House of Representatives Rules of Procedure, 2083
Preface: The House of Representatives has made these Rules of Procedure in exercise of the powers conferred by Article 104, Sub-article (1) of the Constitution of Nepal, to regulate the conduct of business, the formation of committees, the operation and order of the House or its committees, and to remove obstacles as and when they arise.
Chapter-1
Preliminary
9. Brief Name and Commencement: (1) The name of these Rules shall be "House of Representatives Rules of Procedure, 2083".
(2) These Rules shall come into force immediately.
2. Definitions: Unless the subject or context otherwise requires, in these Rules:
(a) "Minister of Finance" means the Minister of Finance of the Government of Nepal, and the word shall also include any other minister or minister of state designated to perform the functions of the Minister of Finance.
(b) "Chairing Member" means a member nominated as per Rule 10 to chair the meeting in the absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker.
(c) "Unparliamentary Word" means a word that is indecent, obscene, objectionable, contrary to public etiquette or morality, and that belittles any person, caste, religion, language, or gender, or is offensive in any other way, discriminatory, demeaning, makes unproven allegations, or reflects geographical discrimination.
(d) "Deputy Speaker" means the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives.
(e) "Senior Member" means the senior member as per Sub-article (5) of Article 91 of the Constitution in the absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker, or when both positions are vacant.
(f) "Table" means the table of the House used to present proposals and information after they have been presented by the proposing member as per these Rules, and the word also includes the act of presenting papers or information to the House.
(g) "Official" means the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Leader of the Opposition in the House of Representatives, Leader of the Parliamentary Party of a political party represented in the House of Representatives, Deputy Leader of the Parliamentary Party of a political party represented in the House of Representatives, Chief Whip, Whip of the ruling party, Whip, and Chairperson.
(h) "Premises" means the premises of the House of Representatives, including the entire building with its chambers and ante-chambers, and the word also includes the place designated by the Speaker as the premises at a specific time.
(i) "House of Representatives" means the House of Representatives as per Article 14 of the Constitution.
(j) "Delegated Legislation" means an order, rule, directive, procedure, or standard issued under delegated authority.
(k) "Motion" means any motion presented to the House of Representatives.
(l) "Proposing Member" means a minister presenting a government bill or any other proposer of a motion as per these Rules.
(m) "Meeting Chamber" means the chamber of the House of Representatives, and the word also includes the visitors' gallery and balcony attached to the meeting chamber.
(n) "Minister" means the Prime Minister, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister, Minister of State, or Assistant Minister of the Government of Nepal.
(o) "Council of Ministers" means the Council of Ministers of the Government of Nepal as per Article 76 of the Constitution.
(p) "Marshal" means the security personnel deployed to maintain order and discipline in the House or committee meetings.
(q) "Secretary-General" means the Secretary-General of the Federal Parliament appointed as per Sub-article (1) of Article 106 of the Constitution, and the word also includes the Secretary of the Secretariat or the senior official designated by the Speaker to perform the functions of the Secretary-General in his absence.
(r) "Secretary" means the Secretary of the House of Representatives appointed as per Sub-article (1) of Article 106 of the Constitution, and the word also includes the Secretary of the Secretariat or the senior official designated by the Speaker to perform the functions of the Secretary in his absence.
(s) "Secretariat" means the Federal Parliament Secretariat as per Article 107 of the Constitution.
(t) "House", "Assembly", or "Meeting" means the House, Assembly, or Meeting of the House of Representatives.
(u) "Member" means a member of the House of Representatives, and the word also includes the minister presenting a motion.
(v) "Treaty" means a treaty or agreement to which the State of Nepal or the Government of Nepal is a party.
(w) "Chairperson" means the Chairperson of a committee.
(x) "Speaker" means the Speaker of the House of Representatives.
(y) "Committee" means a committee formed as per these Rules.
(z) "Notice Paper" means a notice paper that includes the following matters:
(1) Notice regarding the proceedings of the meeting,
(2) Brief record of the proceedings of the meeting,
(3) Notice related to committees,
(4) Any other matter deemed necessary by the Speaker.
(aa) "Constitution" means the Constitution of Nepal.
(bb) "Minister of Parliamentary Affairs" means the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs of the Government of Nepal.
3. Convening and End of Session: (1) The notice of the convening of a session by the President as per Sub-article (1) of Article 93 of the Constitution shall be given to the members by the Secretary-General or, in his absence, by the Secretary.
(2) The end of a session convened as per Sub-article (1) shall be declared by the President as per Sub-article (2) of Article 93 of the Constitution. The notice of such end shall be read out by the Speaker in the meeting. However, if the meeting of the House of Representatives is adjourned, the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall inform the members about the end of the session through a notice paper.
(3) If the House of Representatives is not in session or is adjourned, and if one-fourth of the total number of members of the House of Representatives requests the President in writing, as per Sub-article (3) of Article 93 of the Constitution, to convene a session or meeting, the President shall specify the date and time for such session or meeting.
(4) The notice of convening and ending of a session of the House of Representatives by the President as per Article 93 of the Constitution shall be published in the Nepal Gazette and disseminated through public media as required.
4. Member's Attendance: (1) Before commencing the meeting, each member shall register their attendance in the attendance register kept outside the chamber or in the electronic attendance equipment in the ante-chamber.
(2) The Secretariat may publicly disclose information regarding the attendance of members in the meeting through electronic means.
5. Order of Seating: (1) Members shall take their seats in the order and place determined by the Speaker in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee.
(2) The Speaker may permit a member with a disability to be accompanied by a helper and to sit in a designated place outside the meeting chamber.
6. Operation and Adjournment of Meetings: (1) The meeting shall be held on the day and time specified by the Speaker, keeping in mind the workload of the House.
(2) Generally, the meeting shall commence at 1:00 PM. However, if the Speaker deems it necessary, the meeting may commence up to two hours after the scheduled time. If the meeting cannot commence even after two hours, the Speaker shall adjourn the meeting and announce the next meeting.
(3) If, for any reason, the day, time, or agenda of a meeting is changed, the information shall be posted on the notice board and disseminated to all members through electronic means. Such information shall be deemed to have been received by all members.
(4) The Speaker shall announce the commencement and adjournment of each meeting.
However, if the Speaker is unable to be present in the meeting due to circumstances beyond their control, the Deputy Speaker shall announce the commencement and adjournment of the meeting, or the adjournment of a meeting commenced by the Speaker.
(5) The presence of the concerned minister shall be mandatory in any meeting where discussions are to be held on a subject related to their ministry.
(6) The leaders of the parliamentary parties represented in the House of Representatives shall cooperate in the operation of the House of Representatives.
Chapter-3
Election of Speaker and Deputy Speaker and Nomination of Members to Chair Meetings
7. Election of Speaker: (1) The election of the Speaker shall be held on a day and time specified by the Speaker after the commencement of the session, and the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall publish the notice thereof.
(2) Any member wishing to propose another member for election to the post of Speaker shall submit a notice of proposal in the format specified in Schedule-1 to the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary within the specified time.
(3) After the proposer has spoken, the supporting member shall speak, and a maximum of three supporting members can support the proposal.
(4) If only one proposal is received within the specified time, the proposed member shall be declared Speaker unopposed after the proposer and supporters have spoken. If more than one proposal is received within the specified time, the Speaker shall present the proposals in the order they were received, and after the proposer and supporters have spoken, the person chairing the meeting shall present the proposals for decision in order.
(5) If more than one proposal is presented for decision as per Sub-rule (4), the proposal that secures the majority of the total number of members present in the House of Representatives shall be considered to have passed, and the proposed member shall be declared elected as Speaker. The remaining proposals shall not be presented for decision.
(6) The decision on the proposal shall be made by a division of votes, including signed votes.
(7) If the proposal as per Sub-rule (5) is not passed by a majority in the House of Representatives, a re-election shall be held.
(8) If the member proposed for the post of Speaker is absent, the senior member present shall chair the meeting for that day.
(9) If the post of Speaker becomes vacant for any reason, the Deputy Speaker shall specify the date and time for the election within fifteen days from the date of vacancy if the session is in progress, or within fifteen days from the commencement of the session if the session is not in progress. If the post of Deputy Speaker is also vacant, the senior member shall specify the date and time for the election.
8. Oath: The Speaker and the Deputy Speaker shall take the oath of office and secrecy before the President in the format specified in Schedule-2.
9. Nomination of Members to Chair Meetings: (1) The Speaker may, in consultation with the Deputy Speaker, nominate up to seven members to chair the meetings of the House of Representatives during the session.
(2) The members nominated as per Sub-rule (1) shall be able to exercise all the rights of the Speaker while chairing the meeting.
Chapter-4
Meeting Procedures
10. Days for Government and Non-Government Business: Each day the House of Representatives meets shall be a day for government business, and the time after the Question Hour on Fridays shall be for non-government business. However, if the Speaker deems it necessary, another day may be designated for non-government business if a meeting is not held on a Friday for any reason.
Clarification: For the purpose of this Rule, "Government Business" means any bill, motion, or subject presented to the House by a minister, and "Non-Government Business" means any bill, motion, or subject presented by a member other than a minister.
11. Daily Agenda: (1) As directed by the Speaker, the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall prepare the agenda for the day before the meeting and provide it to the parliamentary party offices and members through electronic means.
(2) As directed by the Speaker, the agenda shall be prepared one hour before the meeting and a copy shall be provided to the members.
(3) Unless otherwise specified in these Rules, no subject not included in the agenda may be considered on any given day without the permission of the Speaker.
12. Business Advisory Committee: (1) A Business Advisory Committee consisting of a maximum of fifteen members, with proportional representation from political parties in the House of Representatives, shall be formed under the chairmanship of the Speaker to advise on the orderly conduct of the meeting, priority and time limits for business, and other necessary matters.
(2) The Deputy Speaker and the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs shall be the ex-officio Vice-Chairperson and member, respectively.
(3) The Speaker may invite any member to attend the meeting of the Business Advisory Committee as a special invitee if the Speaker deems it appropriate.
(4) The Business Advisory Committee shall meet regularly during the session and as needed at other times.
13. Determination of Time Limits: (1) The Speaker shall set the time limit for discussion on the business presented in the meeting.
(2) After the time limit set as per Sub-rule (1) expires, the Speaker shall not allow further discussion and shall present all necessary proposals for decision to the meeting.
14. Zero Hour and Special Time: (1) The Speaker may set aside time for members to present urgent matters of public importance during Zero Hour and Special Time.
However, if a member requests time to draw the government's attention to a serious incident or matter of urgent public importance, the Speaker may grant additional time.
(2) The Speaker may grant additional time for members to draw the government's attention to a serious incident or matter of urgent public importance.
(3) The concerned minister shall provide a response to the issues raised during Zero Hour and Special Time within seven days.
15. Time for Giving Notice: Unless otherwise specified in these Rules, members giving notice shall do so to the Secretary between 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM on the day of the meeting. The notice given within that time shall be considered valid for the next working day.
16. Amendment to Notice: If any word or phrase in a notice is found to be objectionable, sarcastic, unnecessary, inappropriate, or irrelevant, the Speaker may amend or cause it to be amended.
17. Distribution of Papers: (1) The Secretary shall make available necessary papers and information to the members.
(2) The Secretary shall arrange for the distribution of relevant papers and information to the members through their pigeonholes, official email, or the Secretariat's official application. Such distributed papers and information shall be deemed to have been received by the members.
18. Commencement of Meeting: The Speaker shall announce the commencement of the meeting after entering the meeting chamber at the scheduled time.
19. Rules to be Observed in the Meeting: Members shall observe the following rules:
(a) Everyone shall stand and show respect upon entering the meeting chamber.
(b) The Speaker shall show respect to the meeting and take their seat.
(c) Only members shall enter the meeting chamber after the Speaker leaves.
(d) Members shall speak only after being called upon by the Speaker or signaled by them.
(e) When speaking, members shall address the Speaker and speak while standing in the designated place, unless the Speaker orders otherwise.
(f) While the Speaker is addressing the meeting, no member shall leave their seat, and all members shall listen attentively to the Speaker.
(g) No member shall walk between the Speaker's seat and the seat of the member speaking.
(h) Members shall not sit or stand with their backs turned towards the Speaker.
(i) Members shall not do anything that disrupts the order of the meeting or causes disorder.
(j) Members shall not read books, newspapers, or other papers unrelated to the business of the meeting.
(k) Mobile phones shall be kept on silent mode in the meeting chamber, and no calls, photography, or audio/video recording shall be made.
20. Rules to be Observed by Members Participating in Discussions: Members shall observe the following rules:
(a) Members shall stand up to participate in discussions and speak only after their name is called or signaled by the Speaker.
(b) Members shall not criticize the conduct of the Speaker except in the context of a motion related to the Speaker's conduct.
(c) Discussions shall not be held on matters that are prohibited by Article 104 of the Constitution.
(d) Members shall not speak indecently, obscenely, offensively, contrary to public etiquette or morality, or in a way that belittles any person, caste, religion, language, or gender, or use unparliamentary words.
(e) Members shall not misuse their right to speak to obstruct the proceedings of the House.
21. Order of Speaking: Discussions shall proceed as follows:
(a) After the member presenting the motion has spoken, the member whose name is called or signaled by the Speaker shall be allowed to speak.
(b) Unless permitted otherwise by these Rules, no member shall speak more than once on the same motion without the Speaker's permission.
(c) The member presenting the motion shall have the right to speak again at the end of the discussion.
(d) No member shall have the right to answer without the Speaker's permission.
22. Relevance: (1) A member speaking shall be relevant to the subject under consideration.
(2) If a member repeatedly speaks on irrelevant matters or reiterates the arguments of others, the Speaker may draw their attention to the subject and request them to focus on the topic. If they fail to focus on the subject, the Speaker may order them to stop speaking. Upon such an order, the member shall stop speaking and take their seat.
23. Seeking or Giving Clarification: (1) During a discussion, any member may seek clarification on the relevant subject through the Speaker.
(2) Notwithstanding anything written in Sub-rule (1), any member may, with the Speaker's permission, provide clarification on matters related to themselves. However, no controversial issue shall be raised during such clarification.
(3) No further discussion shall take place on the clarification provided as per Sub-rule (2).
24. Conclusion of Discussion: (1) Unless otherwise specified in these Rules, the discussion shall be deemed concluded after the member presenting the motion has given their reply.
(2) The Speaker may declare the discussion concluded if they deem it necessary.
(3) If the Speaker feels that the discussion has been unnecessarily prolonged, they may, after consulting the opinion of the House, set a time for the conclusion of the discussion. Upon the expiry of the time so set, the discussion shall be deemed concluded, and all necessary proposals shall be presented to the meeting for decision.
25. Point of Order: (1) If any member feels that any provision of these Rules has been violated in relation to a matter currently under consideration by the meeting, they may raise a point of order, stating the specific rule that has been violated.
(2) Upon receiving a signal or indication from the Speaker, the member raising the point of order shall stop speaking.
(3) The member raising the point of order shall clearly state the basis for raising the point of order and shall then take their seat.
(4) The Speaker shall decide on the point of order raised in the meeting, and the decision shall be final.
Chapter-4
Methods of Decision Making
26. Decisions by Voting: When the Speaker presents a motion under consideration to the meeting for decision, it shall be presented in the form of a question.
27. Method of Presenting Questions for Decision: (1) After the discussion on the motion is concluded, the Speaker shall present the question to the members, asking them to say "Aye" or "No" in a clear voice.
(2) After the motion is presented for decision as per Sub-rule (1), the Speaker shall announce which side has the majority between "Aye" and "No".
(3) If the Speaker's announcement as per Sub-rule (2) is not objected to as per Rule 29, the Speaker's announcement shall be considered the decision of the House of Representatives.
(4) After a motion has been presented for decision by the Speaker, no further discussion or amendment shall be allowed, nor shall an adjournment motion be presented.
28. Division: (1) If at least ten members rise from their seats to express disagreement with the Speaker's announcement as per Rule 28, Sub-rule (2), the Speaker shall collect votes using one of the following methods:
(a) By asking each member to pronounce the words "Aye", "No", and "I do not vote".
(b) By having members who say "Aye", "No", and "I do not vote" enter the ante-chamber through designated doors and sign the alphabetical roll call list.
(c) By operating an automatic vote recording machine.
(2) Notwithstanding anything written in Sub-rule (1), if the Speaker deems the demand for division unnecessary, they may ascertain the decision of the House by asking the members who say "Aye", "No", and "I do not vote" to stand up in order.
(3) If an automatic vote recording machine is used for vote collection as per Sub-rule (1):
(a) If any member is unable to operate the machine for any reason, the Speaker may ascertain their vote by asking them before announcing the decision.
(b) If a member mistakenly presses the automatic vote recording machine or if the vote count is incorrect due to any reason, the Speaker may correct their vote by drawing the Speaker's attention before announcing the decision.
(4) The Speaker shall announce the result of the vote collection as per Sub-rule (1) or (2), and no one shall object to it immediately.
(5) The Speaker shall have the right to divide any motion into more than one part for voting.
(6) The Speaker shall determine the method of vote collection, including signed votes, and other procedures for division.
Chapter-6
Order in Meetings
29. Warning: The Speaker may warn any member for indecent behavior, and upon receiving a warning, the member shall immediately control their behavior.
30. Expulsion from Meeting: (1) Any member who does not comply with the order as per Rule 29 may be ordered by the Speaker to leave the meeting chamber. Upon receiving such an order, the member shall immediately leave the meeting chamber and shall not be allowed to attend the meeting for the remainder of that day. If such a member does not leave the meeting chamber immediately after receiving the order, the Speaker may order the marshals to remove them from the meeting chamber with their assistance.
(2) A member expelled as per Sub-rule (1) shall not be allowed to participate in the meetings of the House or any committee for the next three days. The Secretary shall inform the concerned committee and parliamentary party about such expulsion.
31. Suspension of Members: (1) The Speaker may name any member who disrespects the Speaker's seat, intentionally obstructs the proceedings of the House, behaves indecently, or intentionally violates or disregards the Constitution or these Rules.
(2) If a motion is presented by any member to suspend the named member from the meeting, the Speaker shall immediately present the motion for decision. No discussion, amendment, or adjournment motion shall be allowed on such a motion.
(3) If the motion as per Sub-rule (2) is passed, the suspended member shall be deemed suspended and shall not be allowed to attend the meetings of the House and committees for a maximum of fifteen days thereafter.
(4) The suspended member shall immediately leave the meeting chamber as per Sub-rule (3).
(5) If the suspended member does not leave the meeting chamber as per Sub-rule (4), the Speaker may order the marshals to remove them from the meeting chamber.
(6) If a member is suspended under this Rule, or if a motion presented by a suspended member is pending, the Secretary shall inform the concerned committee and parliamentary party about the suspension and its revocation.
(7) If a motion presented by a suspended member under Sub-rule (3) is pending, the Speaker may authorize another member to present the motion.
32. Speaker's Special Authority to Maintain Order: (1) Notwithstanding anything written elsewhere in these Rules, if any member disrupts peace, order, and discipline in the meeting chamber, causes physical damage to the meeting chamber, or insults the prestige of the House, the Speaker may order the marshals to immediately expel such a member from the meeting chamber. The Speaker may also order the suspension of such a member for up to fifteen days and order them to pay for any physical damage caused.
(2) A member suspended as per Sub-rule (1) shall not be allowed to attend the meetings of the House or any committee during the period of suspension.
(3) If a member is suspended under this Rule, or if a motion presented by a suspended member is pending, the Secretary shall inform the concerned committee and parliamentary party about the suspension and its revocation.
(4) Notwithstanding anything written elsewhere in these Rules, if any member engages in objectionable, destructive behavior or causes physical damage to the meeting chamber, the Speaker may, after being informed of such an incident, suspend the member for up to fifteen days and order them to pay for any physical damage caused. However, before issuing such an order, the Speaker shall give the concerned member a reasonable opportunity to present their defense.
33. Actions That Can Be Taken: Notwithstanding anything written elsewhere in these Rules, if a member expelled or suspended under these Rules submits a satisfactory explanation or apology, the Speaker may accept the apology or withdrawal of the action and allow the member to participate in the proceedings.
34. Authority to Adjourn Meeting: (1) If there is disorder in the meeting chamber or for any other reason, the Speaker may adjourn the meeting for the remainder of the day or for any specified period.
(2) During such an adjournment, no member shall be allowed to raise any question.
Chapter-7
Address by the President and Policy and Program
35. Address by the President: (1) The President may address the House of Representatives or the joint session of both Houses of Parliament as per Article 94 of the Constitution.
(2) The Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall inform the members about the address made by the President as per Sub-rule (1).
36. Vote of Thanks: (1) After the President's address is tabled in the meeting, the Prime Minister shall move a vote of thanks for the address.
(2) The Speaker shall present the motion of thanks for the President's address, and the motion shall be presented for decision.
(3) The House of Representatives shall pass the motion of thanks and send it to the President.
37. Procedure Regarding Policy and Program: (1) After the President's address and the passage of the vote of thanks, the Prime Minister or, in his absence, any minister designated by him shall consult with the Speaker or any minister designated by him and set the date and time for discussion on the Policy and Program presented by the President. The discussion shall be held on the specified date, based on the proportional representation of political parties in the House.
(2) During the discussion on the Policy and Program presented by the President, the Speaker may propose amendments in a manner deemed appropriate.
(3) At the conclusion of the discussion, the Prime Minister or, in his absence, the designated minister shall answer the questions raised.
(4) After the Prime Minister or the designated minister has answered, the discussion shall be deemed concluded. The Policy and Program, along with any amendments, shall then be presented to the Speaker for decision.
38. Other Business That Can Be Transacted: (1) The following business may also be transacted on the day allocated for discussion on the President's address:
(a) Completing formal business before the commencement of the discussion.
(b) Presenting the estimates of income and expenditure and seeking permission to present supplementary estimates.
(c) Presenting any bill or seeking permission to present a bill.
(2) If a motion to adjourn the discussion is passed, the following business may be transacted on the day allocated for discussion:
(a) Presenting a motion for the passage of any bill.
(b) Presenting matters that have been presented to the meeting according to the law.
(c) Discussing any urgent matter that requires the minister's attention.
Chapter-8
Question and Answer
39. Questions That Can Be Asked: (1) Questions of public importance within the purview of the Government of Nepal and related to any subject may be asked in the meeting.
(2) Questions as per Sub-rule (1) may be registered after the commencement of the session.
40. Question and Answer Time: (1) Unless the Speaker orders otherwise, one hour of the first meeting of each day shall be allocated for Question and Answer.
(2) After the Question and Answer time as per Sub-rule (1) concludes, the other business as per the agenda of the meeting shall commence.
41. Notice of Questions: (1) Any member wishing to ask a question shall provide notice to the Secretary, including the following details:
(a) The question to be asked,
(b) The minister concerned with the question,
(c) In the case of Rule 47, the member concerned.
(2) If more than one member signs the notice of a question, the question submitted by the first signatory member shall be considered. However, if the first signatory member is absent, the question submitted by the next member in order shall be considered.
(3) If more than one member gives notice of a question on the same subject, only the first question registered shall be considered. However, the Speaker shall read out the names of all members who have submitted questions.
42. Types of Questions: (1) Questions shall be of two types: those requiring oral answers and those requiring written answers.
(2) Answers that refer to any record, document, etc., shall be given in writing.
43. List of Questions: (1) After receiving answers from the ministries, a list of questions requiring oral and written answers for each day shall be prepared, and all questions not rejected shall be included in such a list. However, no more than twenty oral questions and fifty written questions shall be included in the list per day. No more than two oral questions related to the same subject shall be included in the list.
(2) The order of questions requiring written answers shall be determined based on the time of receipt and the subject matter.
(3) The order of questions requiring oral answers shall be determined based on the order of registration.
44. Questions Not Answered to be Laid on the Table: (1) If, due to lack of time, a question listed for an oral answer on a particular day cannot be answered, the concerned minister shall lay a copy of the answer on the table. However, if the minister requests the Speaker, stating that answering an unanswered question is necessary in the public interest, the Speaker may allow the answer to be given even after the time allocated for the question has expired.
(2) A copy of the answer laid on the table as per Sub-rule (1) shall be made available to the members.
(3) All oral and written questions for which answers have been received but not answered during the current session shall be laid on the table at the end of the session.
45. Answer to Questions: (1) The Secretariat shall arrange for the dispatch of registered oral and written questions to the concerned ministries within five days.
(2) The concerned ministry shall provide the answers to the oral and written questions as per Sub-rule (1) to the Secretariat within a maximum of five days from the date the questions are received. The Speaker shall manage the time for presenting the answers from the ministries to the meeting after receiving the answers.
(3) A copy of written questions and answers shall be made available to each member.
(4) Other arrangements regarding question and answer sessions shall be made as determined by the Speaker in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee.
46. Questions to be Asked to the Member Presenting the Proposal or Bill: (1) Except for the minister presenting a proposal or bill, questions may be asked to any other member regarding matters related to the proposal or bill.
(2) Regarding questions to be asked to a minister, the Speaker may apply the procedure determined for questions to ministers as per the relevant rules as needed.
47. Conditions Regarding Questions: The following types of questions shall not be acceptable:
(a) Vague questions,
(b) Questions that are too long, baseless, meaningless, or insignificant,
(c) Questions that name or quote any person, unless it is absolutely necessary for clarification, in which case the questioner shall be responsible for the accuracy of the name or statement.
(d) Questions that suggest an answer or opinion, or are intended to promote a particular viewpoint,
(e) Questions that seek information that cannot be provided in a single answer, or are related to policy matters,
(f) Questions containing false expressions, mere arguments, baseless assumptions, sarcasm, accusations, allegations, objectionable, or unparliamentary words,
(g) Questions asking for hypothetical solutions to problems,
(h) Questions related to matters under consideration by a committee or reports submitted by a committee to the House,
(i) Questions on matters that can be easily ascertained through other means.
48. Matters on Which Questions Cannot Be Asked: (1) Questions shall not be asked on the following matters:
(a) Matters prohibited from publication by the Constitution or any prevailing law,
(b) Matters that are inherently confidential or any decision or action of the Council of Ministers that would be contrary to national interest if published,
(c) Matters that criticize the decision of any committee or the House,
(d) Matters that have been clarified through discussion in the current session,
(e) Matters that contain the name of any person or organization for direct or indirect propaganda purposes,
(f) Matters under consideration by any commission or committee formed to investigate, advise, or submit reports as per prevailing laws, or matters under the jurisdiction of judicial or quasi-judicial bodies established as per prevailing laws,
(g) Matters related to the interpretation of laws,
(h) Matters questioning whether a statement by a non-governmental person is true or not,
(i) Matters related to the personal conduct of any person outside their official or public capacity,
(j) A matter on which a question has been asked and rejected once as per these Rules, or a matter on which a decision has been made.
(2) Notwithstanding anything written in clause (g) of Sub-rule (1), the Speaker may allow questions to be asked, limited to the progress of the work of the commission or committee, if it is deemed that such questions will not adversely affect the work of the commission or committee mentioned in that clause.
49. Decision on Whether a Question is Acceptable or Not: (1) The Speaker shall decide whether a question is acceptable or not. If the Speaker finds that the question is being misused or is against the Constitution or these Rules, or is likely to insult the prestige of the House or obstruct the proceedings of the meeting, the Speaker may reject such a question, in whole or in part.
(2) If the Speaker deems it appropriate, they may make necessary amendments to the question to make it conform to the rules, without altering its intent.
(3) Before making amendments as per Sub-rule (2), the Speaker may consult with the member who asked the question.
(4) The Speaker's decision on whether a question is acceptable or not, and whether amendments are to be made, shall be final.
50. Supplementary Questions: (1) If further clarification is needed regarding the oral answer to a question, the member who asked the question may ask a supplementary question.
(2) A supplementary question must be clearly related to the original question.
(3) The conditions regarding questions as per these Rules shall also apply to supplementary questions.
51. Withdrawing or Postponing Questions: (1) A member may withdraw their question at any time before it is included in the agenda.
(2) A member may postpone their question, which is not included in the agenda, to another day by giving notice to the Secretary two days in advance. The postponed question shall be included in the agenda of another day for which it is scheduled. The postponed question shall be included in the agenda of another day for which it is scheduled.
52. Procedure for Question and Answer: (1) After the Question and Answer time begins, the Speaker shall call the name of the questioner member in order.
(2) The member called or the member authorized by them shall stand up in their seat and ask the question as per the question list, stating the intent of the question.
(3) If the question is not asked as per the rules, it shall be deemed automatically removed from the question list.
53. Refusal to Answer: If answering a question is deemed contrary to national interest or public interest, the answer to such a question may be refused.
54. Change of Question: The Speaker may change an oral question if they deem it appropriate. The Speaker may also change a written question.
Chapter-9
Direct Question and Answer with the Prime Minister
55. Direct Questions Can Be Asked: (1) The Speaker shall designate one hour of the first meeting of the first week of each month for direct questions to the Prime Minister regarding matters related to his portfolio or his responsibilities.
However, if the meeting cannot be held on that day for any reason, the first hour of the next meeting shall be designated.
(2) The Speaker shall call the name of the questioner member during the designated time.
(3) The member called as per Sub-rule (2) shall stand up in their seat and ask a question to the Prime Minister.
(4) The Prime Minister shall answer the question as per Sub-rule (3).
(5) In questions under this Rule, a maximum of fifteen members can ask questions in a day's meeting, and after one member has asked a question and received an answer, the name of the next questioner member shall be called in order.
56. Direct Question and Answer Can Be Conducted: The question and answer session under this chapter may be broadcast live through government and other media.
57. Information to be Provided: Members wishing to ask questions under this chapter shall provide written information about their questions to the Speaker three days before the commencement of the meeting.
58. Conditions Regarding Questions Shall Apply: (1) The conditions regarding questions as per this chapter shall also apply to questions under this chapter, and questions on matters prohibited as per Rule 49 shall not be asked.
(2) The decision on whether a question is acceptable or not as per Rule 58 shall be made as per Rule 50.
(3) Other procedures related to question and answer sessions shall be as determined by the Speaker.
59. No Discussion Shall Take Place: No discussion shall take place regarding the answer given under this chapter.
Chapter-10
Procedure Regarding Motions
60. No Discussion Without a Motion: Except as specified in the Constitution and these Rules, no subject shall be discussed in the meeting without a motion.
61. Conditions Regarding Motions: (1) The following types of motions shall not be acceptable:-
(a) Motions that violate Article 104 of the Constitution or any other provision of the Constitution,
(b) Motions that include more than one subject,
(c) Motions that are vague or unclear,
(d) Motions containing mere arguments, assumptions, sarcasm, irrelevance, accusations, or any other speculative or objectionable content,
(e) Motions that mention the personal conduct of any person outside their public or government capacity,
(f) Motions that criticize the decisions of the House of Representatives or its committees, or matters under consideration by a committee,
(g) Motions that mention subjects under consideration by any commission or committee formed to investigate, advise, or submit reports as per prevailing laws, or matters under the jurisdiction of judicial or quasi-judicial bodies established as per prevailing laws,
(h) Motions that repeat discussions held in the current session,
(i) Motions that use indecent and unparliamentary language,
(j) Motions related to incidents of gender-based violence and discrimination, or criminal matters, where confidentiality is not maintained as per law,
(k) Motions related to any decision or action of the Council of Ministers, where national security, integrity, or diplomatic relations may be jeopardized, as certified by the Council of Ministers.
(2) Notwithstanding anything written in clause (g) of Sub-rule (1), the Speaker may permit the presentation of a motion if it is deemed that it will not adversely affect the work of the commission or committee mentioned in that clause, limited to the scope of investigation and progress of work.
62. Decision on Whether a Motion is Acceptable or Not: The Speaker shall decide whether a motion is acceptable or not, and in doing so, the Speaker may reject any part or the entire motion with reasons.
63. Setting the Day and Time for Discussion: (1) The Speaker may set the day and time for discussion on a motion, keeping in mind the workload of the House of Representatives.
(2) After the discussion period set as per Sub-rule (1) expires, the Speaker shall present all necessary proposals for decision to the meeting without allowing further discussion.
64. Motions Becoming Invalid and Not to be Presented Again: (1) A motion for which permission to present has been obtained but which is not presented shall automatically become invalid.
(2) Unless otherwise specified in these Rules, any motion that has been discussed or decided upon in the current session of the House of Representatives shall not be presented again in the same session, even through a different motion, if it pertains to substantially the same subject.
(3) If a motion registered during the current session is not discussed, it shall automatically become invalid. However, if the proposing member submits a request stating that the registered motion is timely and appropriate, the motion shall remain valid as per the Speaker's decision.
65. No Discussion Before the Appointed Time: No motion or amendment shall be presented for discussion before the appointed time or if the matter has already been included in the agenda.
66. Motions Can Be Withdrawn: (1) A motion registered with the Secretariat may be withdrawn by the proposer in writing with the Speaker's permission.
However, a motion that has already been presented to the meeting cannot be withdrawn without permission, and if an amendment has been presented to the motion, the motion cannot be withdrawn until a decision is reached on the amendment.
(2) If more than one member presents substantially the same motion, only the first motion registered or the motion agreed upon by mutual consent shall be discussed.
67. Notice of Motions: A member wishing to present a motion shall give written notice thereof to the Secretary.
68. Procedure to be Adopted Regarding Motions: The procedure specified in this chapter and the relevant chapter of these Rules shall be followed regarding motions. If anything is not specified in the relevant chapter, the provisions of this chapter and Chapter-13 shall apply.
69. Motions Can Be Presented Without Notice: (1) Notwithstanding anything written in this chapter, the following motions may be presented with the Speaker's permission:
(a) Expressing thanks,
(b) Adjourning the meeting,
(c) Withdrawing motions and amendments,
(d) Offering congratulations,
(e) Expressing condolences,
(f) Adjourning the discussion,
(g) Extending the duration of the discussion,
(h) Extending the duration of the meeting,
(i) Special motions.
(2) After the motion as mentioned in Sub-rule (1) is presented to the meeting with the Speaker's permission, the Speaker shall present the motion for the decision of the meeting.
70. Urgent Public Importance Motion: (1) If a member wishes to discuss a matter of urgent public importance, they shall submit a notice of the motion to the Secretary at least two hours before the meeting commences. Such a motion must be supported by at least two members.
(2) The notice of the motion shall clearly state the reason for the urgent public importance. The Speaker shall grant permission to discuss the motion after consulting with the concerned minister.
(3) The Speaker shall set the day and time for discussion on the urgent public importance motion approved as per Sub-rule (3).
(4) The Speaker shall set a time limit of up to two hours for the discussion on the approved motion.
(5) After the proposer member is called by name, the proposer member shall present a brief statement. Thereafter, the Speaker shall allocate time for members to participate in the discussion. The concerned minister shall then provide a response to the issues raised during the discussion.
71. Attention Motion: (1) A member may submit a motion to draw the attention of the concerned minister to a matter of public importance with the Speaker's prior permission.
(2) If the concerned minister wishes, they may request additional time to respond to the attention motion submitted as per Sub-rule (1) on the same day or any other day.
(3) No discussion shall take place on the attention motion after the concerned minister provides a response as per Sub-rule (2). However, the response shall be given at the end of the day.
(4) Members may seek clarification on the attention motion, and the minister shall provide a response. However, more than three members' names shall not be included in a single attention motion.
(5) When drawing the attention of a member, only one member can draw attention at a time, and no more than two attention motions can be presented in a single meeting.
(6) A member wishing to submit a motion shall give notice to the Secretary one day in advance.
(7) Only two motions shall be included in the agenda for a day if approved by the Speaker, out of more than two attention motions submitted in a day.
72. Other Motions Cannot Be Presented: Except for motions as per Rules 70, 71, and 72, no other motion shall be presented under this chapter.
Chapter-11
Adjournment Motion
73. Notice of Adjournment Motion: (1) Subject to these Rules, any member may present a motion to adjourn the meeting to discuss a matter of urgent public importance with the Speaker's permission.
However, if such a motion is not in accordance with the Rules or if the Speaker rejects it, the Speaker shall inform the member of the reasons for rejection.
(2) If the Speaker deems it necessary, they may obtain information from the proposing member or the minister before approving or rejecting the motion.
(3) Notice of the adjournment motion shall be given to the Secretary two hours before the commencement of the meeting on the day the motion is intended to be presented. A copy of the motion along with the notice shall be provided to the Speaker, the concerned minister, and the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs.
(4) Not more than one such motion shall be presented in a meeting.
(5) If more than one member signs the notice of a motion, the notice submitted by the first signatory member shall be considered.
74. Conditions Regarding Adjournment Motion: An adjournment motion can be presented subject to the following conditions:-
(a) The matter or incident must have occurred recently and be of urgent public importance within the responsibility of the Government of Nepal.
(b) The conditions specified in Rule 62 must be met.
75. Permission of the Meeting to Present Adjournment Motion: (1) After the Speaker grants permission to present an adjournment motion as per Rule 74, the Speaker shall call the name of the proposing member at the commencement of the meeting, and then the member wishing to present the adjournment motion shall seek permission from the meeting to present the motion.
(2) If any member opposes the adjournment motion, the Speaker shall ask the opposing and supporting members to stand up. If twenty or more members stand up, the motion shall be deemed to have received permission to be presented.
76. Determination of Time for Discussion on Motion: The Speaker may set a time for discussion on the adjournment motion on the same day.
77. Conclusion of Discussion and Decision: (1) The Speaker shall allow sufficient discussion on the adjournment motion and, after the discussion is concluded, shall present the motion for the decision of the meeting.
(2) If the adjournment motion is rejected, it shall not impede the conduct of the day's agenda.
Chapter-12
Resolution Motion
78. Resolution Motion Can Be Presented: (1) Subject to these Rules, any member may present a resolution motion to:
(a) Express an opinion or recommendation,
(b) Express support or opposition to any action or policy of the Government of Nepal or draw attention for reconsideration,
(c) Give any message or directive.
(2) Notwithstanding anything written in Sub-rule (1), the Speaker may permit the presentation of a resolution motion on any other subject deemed appropriate and necessary.
79. Notice of Resolution Motion: (1) The proposer shall give notice of the resolution motion they wish to present to the Secretary. Such a resolution motion can be discussed in any meeting seven days after it is registered.
(2) The Secretariat shall promptly provide the registered resolution motion to the concerned minister.
(3) No member shall give notice of more than three resolution motions in a single session without the Speaker's permission.
80. Conditions Regarding Resolution Motion: In addition to the conditions mentioned in Rule 62, the conditions specified for motions shall also apply to resolution motions.
81. Decision on Whether a Resolution is Acceptable or Not: (1) The Speaker shall decide whether a resolution motion is acceptable or not. If any resolution or part thereof is contrary to the Constitution or these Rules, the Speaker shall reject it.
(2) A copy of the resolution motion approved by the Speaker shall be distributed to the members within two days for the purpose of presenting amendments.
82. Presentation of Resolution Motion: Not more than one resolution motion shall be included in the agenda of a meeting.
83. Method of Presenting Resolution Motion: (1) After calling the name of the member, the proposer member may present the resolution motion by reading out its details and making a statement.
However, any member may, with the Speaker's permission, authorize another member to present the resolution motion.
(2) After the Speaker calls the name of the member as per Sub-rule (1), if the member wishes not to present the resolution motion, it shall be deemed that they have withdrawn the motion.
84. Time Limit for Discussion: The Speaker shall determine the time limit for discussion on the resolution motion and the response of the concerned minister at the end.
85. Conditions Regarding Amendments: (1) Amendments to resolution motions presented under this chapter may be presented with the Speaker's permission.
(2) The conditions regarding amendments mentioned in Rule 90 shall also apply to resolution motions.
(3) If more than one member gives notice of an amendment, the Speaker shall decide which amendment is appropriate.
86. Decision on Motion: After the discussion on the resolution motion is concluded, the House shall make a decision on the motion, including any amendments.
87. Approved Resolutions to be Sent: Each approved resolution motion shall be sent to the concerned minister.
88. Monitoring and Evaluation of the Implementation of Passed Resolution Motions: (1) The concerned committee shall periodically monitor and evaluate the implementation of resolution motions passed by the House of Representatives within its scope.
(2) The committee shall include its findings on the actual status of monitoring and evaluation in its annual report.
Chapter-13
Amendments to Motions
89. Conditions Regarding Amendments: Amendments to motions shall be presented subject to the following conditions:-
(a) Must be related to the subject of the motion,
(b) Must be in accordance with the principle of the motion,
(c) Must not contradict a decision already made by the House,
(d) Must provide a clear meaning.
90. Notice of Amendments: (1) A member wishing to present an amendment shall give notice of the amendment to the Secretary twenty-four hours before the day the motion is to be considered.
(2) A copy of the notice of each amendment shall be made available to the members. No amendment shall be presented to a motion that has already been presented to the House.
(3) No amendment shall be presented to a motion that has already been presented to the House.
91. Acceptance of Amendments: (1) The Speaker shall have the authority to accept or reject amendments presented to a motion.
(2) The Speaker may ask the concerned member to clarify the purpose of the amendment.
(3) Before presenting the motion with approved amendments for decision, the Speaker shall read out the approved amendments to the House.
Chapter-14
Ordinances
93. Presentation of Ordinances: (1) An ordinance issued as per Article 114 of the Constitution shall be presented to the House of Representatives by the concerned minister after the session is convened.
(2) When presenting an ordinance, the minister shall attach a statement of the circumstances and reasons for issuing the ordinance.
(3) A copy of the ordinance issued as per Sub-rule (1) shall be made available to the Secretariat as soon as possible.
94. Notice to Reject the Ordinance: (1) A member wishing to present a motion to reject an ordinance shall submit such notice to the Secretary within two days of the ordinance being presented. In the absence of the Secretary-General, the Secretary shall receive the notice.
(2) The notice as per Sub-rule (1) shall include the reasons for rejecting the ordinance.
(3) If more than one notice is received as per Sub-rule (1), only one motion shall be selected based on mutual agreement or order of registration.
95. Method of Presenting the Motion to Reject the Ordinance: (1) After receiving the notice, the Speaker shall call the name of the member wishing to present the motion to reject the ordinance. The member shall present the motion by reading out its details and making a statement.
(2) With the Speaker's permission, any other member may be authorized to present the motion.
(3) After the Speaker calls the name of the member as per Sub-rule (1), if the member wishes not to present the motion, it shall be deemed that they have withdrawn the motion.
96. Discussion and Decision on the Motion to Reject the Ordinance: (1) Other members may also participate in the discussion on the motion to reject the ordinance as per this chapter.
(2) At the conclusion of the discussion, the concerned minister shall answer the questions raised.
(3) After the minister provides the answer as per Sub-rule (2), the Speaker shall present the motion to reject the ordinance for decision by the meeting.
97. Decision on Ordinances: (1) If a motion to reject an ordinance is not presented as per this chapter, or if the motion to reject the ordinance is not presented, the Speaker shall grant permission to the concerned minister to present a motion to approve the ordinance.
(2) The motion to approve the ordinance as per Sub-rule (1) shall be presented to the meeting for decision.
98. Bill to Replace Approved Ordinances: (1) A bill shall be presented to replace the provisions of an approved ordinance, either as they are or with amendments, along with a statement of the circumstances and reasons for issuing the ordinance immediately.
(2) The procedure for presenting and passing a bill to replace an ordinance as per Sub-rules (1) and (2) shall be as per the procedure for presenting and passing bills.
(3) The bill to replace the ordinance shall be passed within the period specified by Article 114 of the Constitution and presented to the President for certification.
Chapter-15
Management Procedures
99. Notice for Permission to Present a Bill: (1) Subject to the Constitution and these Rules, any member may present a bill. The member wishing to present a bill shall submit a notice to the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary, along with the bill's objective and reasons, conceptual framework, explanatory notes, commentary on delegated legislation, and other necessary documents.
(2) If a bill, upon becoming an Act, incurs financial expenditure, a detailed economic impact assessment shall also be attached to the bill.
100. Dependent Bills Can Be Presented: A dependent bill may be presented even before the main bill is passed, either in full or in part. However, the dependent bill shall not be considered until the main bill is passed.
101. Bills on the Same Subject Not to be Included in the List: Unless the Speaker orders otherwise, any other bill with the same subject and objective as a bill under consideration shall not be included in the list, whether presented before or after the bill under consideration.
102. Commentary on Delegated Legislation: If there is a provision delegating the authority to make laws, a detailed commentary shall be mandatorily attached explaining the reason, nature, and scope of the law, and the potential impact of the delegated legislation.
103. Distribution of Bills: After a bill is registered, a copy of the bill shall be made available to each member within two days for government bills and four days for non-government bills. The bill shall also be posted on the website on the same day.
104. Notice of Opposition to the Motion Seeking Permission to Present a Bill: A member wishing to oppose a motion seeking permission to present a bill shall give notice to the Secretary at least two days before the day the motion is to be presented.
105. Motion Seeking Permission to Present a Bill: (1) A motion seeking permission to present a bill may be presented in any meeting of the House of Representatives seven days after the notice is given. However, a motion seeking permission to present a government bill may be presented seven days in advance.
(2) If any member opposes the motion seeking permission to present a bill, the Speaker shall allow the opposing member and the proposer member to make brief statements respectively. Thereafter, the Speaker shall present the motion for decision without further discussion.
(3) If permission to present a bill is granted as per Sub-rule (2), the proposing member shall immediately present the bill to the House.
(4) Notwithstanding anything written elsewhere in these Rules, if a bill originates in the National Assembly and is sent to the House of Representatives, the proposing member may present a motion to consider the bill as per Rule 105.
106. General Discussion on the Bill: (1) In the meeting following the presentation of the bill, the proposing member or any other member may present one of the following motions:
(a) That the bill be considered,
(b) That the bill be circulated for public opinion.
(2) If the proposing member presents a motion as per clause (a) or (b) of Sub-rule (1), any other member may present another motion as per the same sub-rule. Such a motion shall be presented to the meeting for decision immediately.
(3) During the discussion on the motion as per Sub-rule (1) (a), only the theoretical aspect of the bill shall be discussed. Except for clarifying the intent of the bill, no discussion shall be held on the clauses of the bill, and no amendments may be presented to the bill.
107. Procedure for Obtaining Public Opinion: If a motion to circulate the bill for public opinion is approved as per Rule 106, the Secretary shall specify the period for collecting opinions, publish the bill in the Nepal Gazette, and publicize it through other appropriate means. The opinions collected within the specified period shall be compiled and provided to the proposing member through the Speaker.
(2) Other procedures for obtaining public opinion on a bill shall be as determined by the Speaker.
108. Procedure After Obtaining Public Opinion: After obtaining public opinion as per Sub-rule (1) of Rule 108, the proposing member may present a motion to the House for consideration of the bill along with the public opinion.
109. Conclusion of General Discussion: (1) After the general discussion on the bill is concluded, the proposing member may present one of the following motions:
(a) That the bill be considered clause by clause,
(b) That the bill be sent to a committee for clause-by-clause discussion.
(2) If the proposing member presents a motion as per clause (a) or (b) of Sub-rule (1), any other member may present another motion as per the same sub-rule. Such a motion shall be presented to the meeting for decision immediately.
110. Motions Can Be Authorized to be Presented: (1) If the proposing member is unable to be present, the Speaker may authorize any other member to present the bill, subject to the Speaker's satisfaction.
(2) In the case of a non-government bill passed by the National Assembly and sent to the House of Representatives, the Speaker may authorize any member of the House to present a motion for consideration of the bill.
111. Notice of Amendment to the Bill: Any member wishing to present an amendment to a bill shall give notice of the amendment to the Secretary within seventy-two hours after the conclusion of the general discussion on the bill.
112. Conditions Regarding Amendments: (1) Amendments to bills may be presented subject to the following conditions:-
(a) Must be related to the subject of the bill,
(b) Must be in accordance with the principle of the bill,
(c) Must be clear and meaningful,
(d) Must be related to the clause for which amendment is sought,
(e) Must be in accordance with the principle or decision previously made by the House,
(f) Must clearly state the proposed amendment or vocabulary.
(2) The Speaker shall have the authority to accept, reject, or ask the concerned member to improve any amendment, or to consolidate and accept amendments with similar intent.
113. Details of Amendments: (1) A consolidated list of amendments approved by the Speaker shall be prepared in order of clauses, as far as possible.
(2) A copy of the consolidated list of approved amendments shall be made available to the members and shall also be posted on the website on the same day.
114. Clause-by-Clause Discussion with Amendments: (1) The discussion on the clauses of the bill shall generally be held in order, and the member called by the Speaker or the member authorized by them may present the amendment.
(2) For each clause, whether it remains as passed or an amendment is accepted, the Speaker shall present a motion to the meeting stating, "Let this clause be part of the bill."
However, for the sake of time efficiency, the Speaker may allow discussion on a clause or related amendments collectively to avoid repetition, and may present parts or clauses of the bill for discussion in a different order during the clause-by-clause discussion.
Clarification: Notwithstanding anything written elsewhere in these Rules, for the purposes of this Rule and Rules 118 and 119, "Speaker" shall mean the Chairperson of the concerned committee, and "Meeting" shall mean the meeting of the concerned committee.
115. Amendments Can Be Withdrawn: (1) A member may withdraw an amendment with the Speaker's permission.
However, if an amendment has been presented to an amendment, the original amendment cannot be withdrawn until a decision is reached on the amendment.
(2) If the proposer of an amendment is absent, they may authorize another member to present or withdraw their amendment with the Speaker's permission.
116. Discussion on Schedules: Discussion on schedules and amendments thereto in the bill shall take place immediately after the conclusion of the discussion on the relevant clauses, and the questions presented for decision shall also be presented in the same order.
117. Clauses Can Be Presented for Decision Collectively: The Speaker may, if deemed appropriate, present clauses, schedules, or amended clauses or schedules of the bill for decision collectively.
However, any member may request that a clause or schedule, or an amended clause or schedule, be presented separately for decision, and the Speaker may allow it if the request is deemed appropriate.
118. Presentation of Preamble and Title: After the decision on all other clauses and schedules of the bill has been made, the Speaker shall present the preamble and title clauses for inclusion in the bill, either in their original or amended form.
119. Directions Can Be Given: When a bill is under consideration in the House, the House may direct the concerned committee to expand or include or exclude any specific provision of the bill, provided that such direction does not contradict the original spirit of the bill.
120. Committee Report: After the clause-by-clause discussion on the bill is concluded in the committee and the procedure under Rule 118 is completed, the Chairperson or, in his absence, the nominated member of the concerned committee shall present the bill along with the report to the meeting.
121. Bills Can Be Withdrawn: (1) A member wishing to present a motion seeking permission to withdraw a bill shall give notice one day in advance.
(2) If a motion seeking permission to withdraw a bill is presented while the bill is under consideration by the concerned committee, the concerned committee shall submit a report to that effect to the meeting.
(3) The proposing member may present a motion to withdraw the bill with the Speaker's permission. If any member opposes the motion, the Speaker shall allow the proposing member and the opposing member to make brief statements, and thereafter, without allowing further discussion, shall present the motion for decision to the House.
(4) If the bill originates in the National Assembly and is sent to the House of Representatives for consideration, the proposing member may present a motion seeking the concurrence of the National Assembly. If such a motion is passed and the National Assembly concurs, the proposing member may present a motion to withdraw the bill.
122. Procedure After Presentation of Committee Report: (1) After the committee report is presented, the report shall be distributed to the members.
(2) Unless the Speaker orders otherwise, the proposing member may present one of the following motions in any meeting held twenty-four hours after the distribution of the report:-
(a) That the bill be considered along with the report,
(b) That the bill be sent back to the concerned committee for reconsideration with directions.
(3) If the proposing member presents a motion as per Sub-rule (2), any other member may present another motion as per the same sub-rule.
(4) If a motion is presented as per Sub-rule (3), the Speaker shall give an opportunity to speak to the proposing member and the member presenting the motion. After both have spoken, if the proposing member does not withdraw the motion, the Speaker shall present the motion for decision to the House without allowing further discussion.
(5) If the decision is made to send the bill back to the committee for reconsideration, the concerned committee shall reconsider the bill and submit its report to the meeting as soon as possible.
(6) After the committee submits its report as per Sub-rule (5), the proposing member may present a motion as per clause (a) of Sub-rule (2) in any meeting specified by the Speaker.
(7) If the motion as per Sub-rule (2) (a) is passed, discussion may be held only on the clauses of the bill and related incidental matters, in accordance with the committee's report.
123. Motion to Pass the Bill: After the clause-by-clause discussion on the bill in the meeting and the discussion on the committee report are concluded, and after amendments have been presented for decision to the House, the proposing member shall present a motion to pass the bill.
124. Bills to be Removed from the List: (1) A bill shall be removed from the list in the following circumstances:-
(a) If the motion presented by the proposing member to:
(1) Obtain permission to present the bill,
(2) Consider the bill along with the committee's report,
(3) Pass the bill with or without amendments,
is rejected by the House.
(b) If the bill is withdrawn.
(c) If the proposing member of a non-government bill ceases to be a member of the House.
(d) If the proposing member of a non-government bill becomes a minister.
(2) No motion shall be presented to the meeting regarding a bill removed from the list as per Sub-rule (1).
125. Bills Cannot Be Presented Again: A bill rejected by the House in a session shall not be presented again in the same session.
126. Bills to be Sent to the National Assembly: (1) A bill passed by the House of Representatives shall be sent to the National Assembly with a message.
(2) The Secretary shall certify the bill to be sent to the National Assembly as per Sub-rule (1), indicating the date it was passed by the House.
(3) The Speaker shall certify the first page of a finance bill as a finance bill.
127. Message of Bill Passed by the National Assembly: After receiving the message of a bill passed by the National Assembly, the Secretary shall table it in the House if the session is in progress, and publish it in the notice paper if the session is not in progress.
128. Finance Bill Returned by the National Assembly with Suggestions: (1) After receiving the message of a finance bill passed by the National Assembly and returned with suggestions, the Secretary shall table it in the House as soon as possible, and a copy thereof shall be distributed to the members.
(2) After the copy of the message is distributed, the concerned minister may present a motion in the meeting to consider the suggestions from the National Assembly.
(3) The Speaker may adopt any procedure deemed appropriate when making a decision regarding the suggestions from the National Assembly.
(4) The suggestions deemed appropriate by the decision of the House shall be incorporated into the finance bill, and the Speaker shall present it to the President for certification. The National Assembly shall be informed accordingly.
129. Finance Bill Returned by the National Assembly Without Suggestions or Not Returned Within the Period: (1) If the National Assembly returns a finance bill without suggestions, the Secretary shall table the message from the National Assembly in the House.
(2) If the National Assembly does not return the finance bill within fifteen days, the Speaker shall inform the National Assembly accordingly.
(3) The Speaker shall present the finance bill as per Sub-rule (1) or (2) to the President for certification as soon as possible.
130. Other Bills Returned by the National Assembly with Amendments: (1) After receiving the message of other bills passed by the National Assembly and returned with amendments, the Secretary shall table them in the House as soon as possible, and a copy of the message with amendments shall be distributed to the members.
(2) After the copy of the message with amendments is distributed, the proposing member or the member authorized by them may present a motion in the meeting to consider the amendments.
(3) The Speaker may adopt any procedure deemed appropriate when making a decision on the motion as per Sub-rule (2).
(4) If the House agrees with the amendments made by the National Assembly, the Speaker shall present the bill to the President for certification as soon as possible.
131. Bills Whose Amendments Were Not Accepted by the House: If the House decides not to accept amendments made by the National Assembly to a bill passed by the House and returned with suggestions, the Speaker shall present the bill to the President for certification.
132. Bills Originating in the National Assembly and Passed: (1) A bill originating in the National Assembly and passed by it shall be sent to the House of Representatives with a message. The Secretary shall table it in the House, and a copy thereof shall be distributed to the members.
(2) After the copy of the bill with the message is distributed, the proposing member may present a motion for consideration of the bill in any meeting held two days after the distribution. However, if the Speaker deems it appropriate, they may grant permission to present such a motion in any meeting after the distribution of the bill with the message.
(3) During the discussion on the motion as per Sub-rule (2), the discussion shall be limited to the theoretical aspect of the bill. Unless necessary to clarify the intent of the bill, no discussion shall be held on the clauses.
(4) The procedure for considering a bill originating in the House of Representatives shall apply to the consideration of a bill originating in the National Assembly and sent to the House.
(5) If the motion to consider the bill or the motion to pass the bill with amendments is rejected, or if the bill is passed or passed with amendments, the Secretary shall inform the National Assembly accordingly, clearly stating the details.
133. Speaker's Authority to Correct Errors: The Speaker may correct numerical order, necessary incidental errors, or printing errors that occur in a bill passed by the House.
134. Certification of Bills: (1) The Speaker shall certify the bill as per Sub-article (1) of Article 113 of the Constitution.
(2) When certifying a bill as per Sub-article (1), the Speaker shall also certify whether it is a finance bill.
135. Certification of Bills: (1) The bill certified as per Rule 135 shall be presented to the President for certification as per Sub-article (2) of Article 913 of the Constitution.
(2) After receiving the notice of certification by the President, the Speaker shall read it out in the meeting. If the session is in progress, the Secretary shall publish the notice in the notice paper. If the session is not in progress, the notice shall be made public through electronic means.
(3) The status of the bill shall be made public through electronic means by the Secretariat from the date of its registration until its certification.
136. Bill Returned by the President with a Message: (1) If a bill is returned by the President with a message for reconsideration as per Sub-article (3) of Article 113 of the Constitution, the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall inform the House. If the session is not in progress, the information shall be published in the notice paper.
(2) After receiving information regarding a bill returned by the President with a message, a member may present one of the following motions in any meeting:
(a) That the bill be reconsidered,
(b) That the bill be sent to the concerned committee for reconsideration.
(3) Other procedures related to the bill shall be as per this chapter.
137. Laws Made Under Delegated Management: (1) Laws made under delegated authority shall be made available to the committee of the House of Representatives within fifteen days of their publication in the Nepal Gazette.
(2) The concerned committee shall test the laws made under delegated legislation on the basis of the matters mentioned in the relevant rules.
(3) If the laws made under delegated authority are found to deviate from the scope of the delegated authority, the committee may direct that such provisions be not implemented or be revised and resubmitted.
138. Measurement of Law Implementation: (1) The concerned committee may measure the implementation of laws that have been in effect for at least two years to identify their effectiveness or any problems in implementation and suggest improvements.
(2) The procedure for measuring law implementation shall be as determined by the Speaker.
139. Procedure for Constitution Amendment Bill: (1) A constitution amendment bill received as per Article 274 of the Constitution shall be published by the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary for public information within thirty days of its presentation to the House. However, a constitution amendment bill originating in the National Assembly and received with a message shall not be published as per this sub-rule.
(2) The bill published as per Sub-rule (1) may be presented in any meeting held seven days after the publication.
(3) Notwithstanding anything written in Sub-rule (2), if the bill is to be sent to the Provincial Assemblies for concurrence as per Sub-article (4) and Schedule-6 of Article 274 of the Constitution, it shall be sent within the specified period. However, a bill that does not require to be sent to the Provincial Assemblies for concurrence as per Sub-rule (1) may be presented in any meeting after its presentation as per Sub-rule (2).
(4) If the majority of the Provincial Assemblies reject the bill within the period specified by Sub-article (5) of Article 274, the bill shall become invalid, and further proceedings on that bill shall not be carried out. If information is not received within the period as per Sub-article (5) of Article 274, the proposing member may present a motion for consideration in any meeting held after the expiry of that period. However, for bills that do not require to be sent to the Provincial Assemblies for concurrence as per Sub-rule (3), the proposing member may present a motion for consideration in any meeting after its presentation as per Sub-rule (2).
(5) After the motion as per Sub-rule (4) is approved, amendments may be presented to the bill, limited to the points where amendments have been proposed, specifying the article, sub-article, clause, sub-clause, or provision of the Constitution.
(6) If the motion as per Sub-rule (4) is approved, the Speaker may form a special committee to discuss the bill clause by clause and present the bill with the report to the House.
(7) The Speaker shall present each article or sub-article of the constitution amendment bill and any amendments thereto for decision in the meeting.
(8) A motion to pass the constitution amendment bill shall be deemed passed if it receives at least two-thirds majority of the total members present in the House of Representatives.
(9) The decision on the motion to pass the constitution amendment bill shall be made by a division of votes, including signed votes.
(10) If a constitution amendment bill passed by the House is received from the National Assembly with a message, and if the total votes in favor reach at least two-thirds of the total members present in both Houses, the Speaker shall certify the constitution amendment bill and send it to the President for certification.
(11) Other procedures for constitution amendment bills shall be as per this chapter and these Rules.
Chapter-16
Procedure Regarding Estimates of Income and Expenditure
142. Estimates of Income and Expenditure: (1) The Minister of Finance shall present the annual estimates of income and expenditure of the Federal Parliament in the meeting.
(2) After the annual estimates of income and expenditure are presented as per Sub-rule (1), the Minister of Finance shall table a copy of the annual estimates of income and expenditure in the meeting.
(3) Discussion shall not be held on the annual estimates of income and expenditure on the day they are tabled.
