143. Discussion on Annual Estimates of Income and Expenditure: (1) Before presenting the Finance Bill to the meeting, the Minister of Finance shall present a motion for general discussion on the annual estimates of income and expenditure.
(2) The Speaker shall set the date and time for the general discussion on the annual estimates of income and expenditure in consultation with the Prime Minister or any minister designated by him in his absence.
(3) The general discussion on the annual estimates of income and expenditure shall be held on the date and time specified as per Sub-rule (2). At the conclusion of the discussion, the Minister of Finance shall answer the questions raised.
144. Supplementary Estimates: (1) The Minister of Finance may present supplementary estimates in the meeting of the House of Representatives as per Article 121 of the Constitution.
(2) When presenting supplementary estimates as per Sub-rule (1), the Minister of Finance shall clarify their objective, reasons, and scope.
(3) Discussion shall not be held on supplementary estimates on the day they are presented.
(4) The Speaker shall set the date and time for the general discussion on supplementary estimates in consultation with the Prime Minister or any minister designated by him in his absence.
(5) The discussion shall be held on the date and time specified as per Sub-rule (4).
(6) The discussion on supplementary estimates shall commence as per Sub-rule (4), and at the conclusion of the discussion, the Minister of Finance shall answer the questions raised.
145. Expenditure Estimates: (1) The amount of expenditure proposed for each ministry shall generally be listed under separate headings. However, the Minister of Finance may include the expenditure proposed for two or more ministries and departments under a single heading, or include expenditure that cannot be easily classified under a particular ministry under a single heading.
(2) A detailed description of the proposed expenditure, divided into sub-headings, shall be included under each heading. Discussion may be held on such descriptions.
However, approval shall not be required for expenditure from the Consolidated Fund.
Chapter-17
Procedure Regarding Appropriation and Finance Bills
146. Procedure Regarding Appropriation Bill: (1) Notwithstanding anything written elsewhere in these Rules, the procedure specified in this chapter shall be followed regarding the Appropriation Bill.
(2) Before presenting the Appropriation Bill, the Minister of Finance shall present a motion for discussion on the principles and priorities of the budget preparation for the Appropriation Bill (excluding the Finance Bill).
(3) The procedure for the discussion shall be as determined by the Speaker in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee.
(4) The discussion as per Sub-rule (2) shall be completed at least fifteen days before the presentation of the annual estimates of income and expenditure.
(5) The report prepared by the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary, incorporating the subject matter discussed as per Sub-rule (2), shall be promptly sent to the Council of Ministers, the Ministry of Finance, and the National Planning Commission. The Ministry of Finance shall prepare the Appropriation Bill based on this report.
(6) After the conclusion of the discussion on the annual estimates as per Sub-rule (2), the Minister of Finance shall present the Appropriation Bill based on the discussion.
(7) After the motion "That the Appropriation Bill be considered" is presented, the Speaker shall set the date and time for discussion and decision on the bill in consultation with the Prime Minister or any minister designated by him in his absence.
(8) The Appropriation Bill shall be discussed and decided upon under various headings, either individually or collectively, as specified.
(9) At the conclusion of the discussion on each heading, the concerned minister shall answer the questions raised.
(10) Before presenting any heading for decision, if there are more than one motion for reduction of expenditure related to that heading, only one motion of the same nature shall be discussed and decided upon.
(11) If separate motions are presented regarding the expenditure amount of the same heading, discussion shall be held in order.
(12) After the conclusion of the discussion on the date and time specified as per Sub-rule (7), the Speaker shall present all remaining headings for decision without discussion.
(13) After the decision is made as per Sub-rule (12), the Minister of Finance shall present a motion to pass the Appropriation Bill. If such a motion is passed, the Appropriation Bill shall be deemed to have been passed.
147. Motion for Reduction of Expenditure: (1) A motion for reduction of expenditure may be presented as follows:-
(a) That the expenditure amount of a heading be reduced to one rupee and maintained as such.
(b) That the expenditure amount of a heading be reduced.
(c) That the expenditure amount of a heading be reduced by one hundred rupees.
(2) A motion presented as "That the expenditure amount of a heading be reduced to one rupee and maintained as such" shall be considered as expressing disagreement with the policy underlying the heading. The member wishing to discuss shall provide a clear and accurate notice stating the specific point of disagreement with the policy and may suggest an alternative policy.
(3) A motion presented as "That the expenditure amount of a heading be reduced" shall be considered as adopting the principle of frugality. Discussion shall be limited to the specific point mentioned in the notice. It is possible to discuss reducing or abolishing a sub-heading or the total expenditure amount of a sub-heading.
(4) A motion presented as "That the expenditure amount of a heading be reduced by one hundred rupees" shall be considered as expressing dissatisfaction with the Government of Nepal regarding a matter within its responsibility. Discussion shall be limited to the specific point mentioned in the notice.
148. Conditions Regarding Motion for Reduction of Expenditure: The following conditions must be met for a motion for reduction of expenditure to be acceptable:-
(a) Must relate to only one heading,
(b) Must clearly state a specific matter of concern,
(c) Must relate to the expenditure amount of the Government of Nepal within its area of responsibility,
(d) Must not relate to the Consolidated Fund,
(e) Must not raise a matter that has already been discussed at a time appointed for discussion in a meeting.
149. Notice of Motion for Reduction of Expenditure: A member wishing to present a motion for reduction of expenditure on any heading shall give notice after the general discussion on the bill is concluded. Only one notice shall be given from a political party or an independent member to a ministry on a given day.
150. Decision on Motion for Reduction of Expenditure: The Speaker shall decide whether a motion for reduction of expenditure is acceptable or not. If the motion is found to be contrary to these Rules, the Speaker may allow it to be amended and accepted.
151. Restriction on Presenting Amendments to Motions for Reduction of Expenditure: Amendments cannot be presented to a motion for reduction of expenditure on any heading.
152. Advance Expenditure Bill: (1) The Minister of Finance may present an advance expenditure bill in the meeting as per Sub-article (1) of Article 122 of the Constitution.
(2) The procedure deemed appropriate by the Speaker shall be followed regarding the advance expenditure bill.
(3) The procedure for presenting and passing a bill as per Sub-article (1) shall be the same as for the advance expenditure bill.
153. Finance Bill: (1) After the annual estimates are presented to the meeting, the Minister of Finance shall present the Finance Bill prepared by the Government of Nepal for implementation.
(2) Notwithstanding anything written elsewhere in these Rules, the procedure specified in this Rule shall be followed regarding the Finance Bill.
(3) After the motion "That the Finance Bill be considered" is presented and approved, the Speaker shall set the date and time for discussion on the bill in consultation with the Prime Minister or any minister designated by him in his absence.
(4) During the discussion on the Finance Bill, any member may discuss matters related to administrative actions of the Government of Nepal, problems of local governments, or monetary and economic policies.
(5) Other procedures related to the Finance Bill shall be as determined by the Speaker as appropriate.
154. Supplementary Appropriation Bill: (1) After the discussion on supplementary estimates is concluded in the meeting, the Minister of Finance shall present the Supplementary Appropriation Bill.
(2) The procedure for appropriation bills shall be followed regarding the Supplementary Appropriation Bill.
155. Loan Expenditure Bill: (1) The Minister of Finance may present a loan expenditure bill in the meeting as per Article 123 of the Constitution.
(2) The procedure deemed appropriate by the Speaker shall be followed regarding the presentation of the bill.
Chapter-18
Vote of Confidence and No-Confidence Motion
156. Vote of Confidence: (1) The Prime Minister appointed as per Sub-article (2), (3), or (5) of Article 76 of the Constitution, or if the party representing the Prime Minister splits or the coalition partners withdraw their support, the Prime Minister shall present a motion seeking a vote of confidence from the House of Representatives within thirty days of such split or withdrawal of support.
(2) At any time, if the Prime Minister deems it necessary to clarify that they have the confidence of the House of Representatives, they may submit a notice to the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary, seeking a vote of confidence.
(3) After receiving the notice as per Sub-rule (1) or (2), the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall submit it to the Speaker, and the Speaker shall specify the date and time for presenting the motion in any meeting after receiving such notice.
(4) The Prime Minister may present the motion in the meeting of the House after obtaining the Speaker's permission and presenting their statement in this regard.
(5) The Speaker shall determine the time limit for discussion on the motion as per Sub-rule (4). At the conclusion of the allocated time, the Prime Minister or a minister authorized by him shall answer the questions raised during the discussion if the Prime Minister is unable to attend the meeting due to illness or circumstances beyond their control.
(6) After the Prime Minister or the minister authorized by him provides the answer as per Sub-rule (5), the Speaker shall present the motion of confidence or no-confidence to the meeting for decision.
(7) The decision on the motion of confidence shall be made by a division of votes, including signed votes.
(8) If the Prime Minister fails to obtain a vote of confidence as per this Rule, the Speaker shall inform the President accordingly.
157. No-Confidence Motion: (1) As per Sub-article (4) of Article 100 of the Constitution, one-fourth of the total members of the House of Representatives may submit a written notice to the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary, stating that they have no confidence in the Prime Minister.
(2) After receiving the notice as per Sub-rule (1), the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall immediately inform the Speaker.
(3) The Speaker shall specify the date and time for discussion on the no-confidence motion in any meeting seven days after receiving the notice as per Sub-rule (1), and the information shall be published in the notice paper.
(4) On the date and time specified as per Sub-rule (3), the first signatory member of the notice or the member authorized by them shall present the motion in the meeting after their name is called by the Speaker. If they wish, they may present their statement regarding the motion before presenting it.
(5) The Speaker shall determine the time limit for discussion on the motion as per Sub-rule (4). At the conclusion of the allocated time, the Prime Minister or a minister authorized by him shall answer the questions raised during the discussion if the Prime Minister is unable to attend the meeting due to illness or circumstances beyond their control.
(6) After the Prime Minister or the minister authorized by him provides the answer as per Sub-rule (5), the proposing member may withdraw the motion with the Speaker's permission.
(7) If the proposing member does not withdraw the motion as per Sub-rule (6), the Speaker shall present the motion for decision to the meeting.
(8) The decision on the no-confidence motion shall be made by a division of votes, including signed votes.
(9) If the no-confidence motion is passed, the Speaker shall inform the President accordingly.
Chapter-19
Motion of Impeachment
158. Motion of Impeachment Against the President or Vice-President: (1) A motion of impeachment against the President or Vice-President as per Sub-article (1) of Article 101 of the Constitution shall be presented stating the grounds and reasons for impeachment and providing the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary with notice thereof.
(2) If the House of Representatives is not in session, the member presenting the motion shall request the convening of a session as per Sub-article (3) of Article 93 of the Constitution within a maximum of five days from the date the motion is registered, specifying the date and time for the meeting.
(3) After receiving the motion as per Sub-rule (1), the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall submit it to the Speaker. If the motion is registered during a session, the date and time for discussion shall be specified within seven days, and if the session is not in progress, the first meeting after the session is convened shall be scheduled.
(4) As per Sub-rule (3), after the Speaker calls the name, the proposing member shall present the motion of impeachment in the meeting. If they wish, they may present a statement before presenting the motion.
(5) After the motion is presented as per Sub-rule (4), the Speaker shall determine the time limit for discussion on the motion. After the discussion is concluded, the proposing member may withdraw the motion with the Speaker's permission.
(6) If the motion is not withdrawn as per Sub-rule (5), the Speaker shall present the motion for decision to the meeting.
(7) The Speaker may, in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee, present a motion to form an eleven-member investigation committee.
(8) If a motion to form an investigation committee as per Sub-rule (6) is passed, the Speaker shall send the motion along with the necessary documents to the investigation committee within three days. The concerned committee and the House shall be informed accordingly.
(9) The investigation committee shall collect evidence regarding serious violations of the Constitution and federal laws by the President or Vice-President and shall have the authority to question the President or Vice-President and collect evidence as needed.
(10) The members of the investigation committee shall elect a chairperson from among themselves.
159. Committee's Term of Office: The term of office of the investigation committee shall be a maximum of three months from the date it commences its investigation.
160. Committee's Procedure for Investigation: (1) After receiving the motion of impeachment, the investigation committee shall commence its investigation as soon as possible.
(2) After commencing the investigation as per Sub-rule (1), the committee shall provide the accused official with a reasonable opportunity to present their defense within seven days and shall conduct the investigation after collecting all facts.
(3) If the accused official does not appear or fails to present their defense within the specified period, the committee shall submit its report with recommendations for impeachment.
(4) The investigation committee shall submit its report with recommendations within a maximum of three months from the date it commences its investigation.
(5) The investigation committee shall manage its internal procedures itself.
161. Committee's Report: (1) The investigation committee shall submit its report with recommendations to the House after completing its investigation.
(2) After the report is submitted to the meeting, a copy of the report shall be distributed to all members.
162. Consideration of Committee's Report: (1) The Speaker shall specify the date and time for the consideration of the investigation committee's report, which shall be presented within forty-eight hours after the report is submitted. The Chairperson of the committee or, in his absence, any member designated by the Speaker, shall present a motion for consideration of the committee's report.
(2) After the motion as per Sub-rule (1) is presented, the report shall be discussed in the meeting.
(3) During the discussion as per Sub-rule (2), any member may present a motion to send the report back to the investigation committee for further investigation regarding any specific matter.
(4) If the motion to send the report back to the investigation committee as per Sub-rule (3) is approved, the report shall be sent to the committee, and the committee shall re-examine it and submit its report to the meeting within seven days.
163. Motion to Approve the Report of the Impeachment Recommendation Committee: (1) After the conclusion of the discussion on the report as per Rule 162, or after the investigation committee's report is resubmitted to the meeting as per Sub-rule (4) of the same Rule, the Chairperson of the committee or, in his absence, any member designated by the Speaker, may present a motion to approve the recommendations mentioned in the report.
(2) If a motion is presented as per Sub-rule (1), any member may present an amendment to the report, if the Speaker deems it appropriate.
(3) After the discussion on the motion presented as per Sub-rule (1) and any amendments presented as per Sub-rule (2), the Speaker shall finalize the amendments and present the report with the approved recommendations to the meeting for decision.
(4) The decision on the motion of impeachment shall be made by a division of votes, including signed votes.
(5) If the motion of impeachment against any official is passed by at least two-thirds majority of the total members present in the House of Representatives, the concerned official shall be deemed removed from office.
(6) The Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall inform the President, the Prime Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the concerned official about the decision of the motion of impeachment.
(7) If the President or Vice-President removed from office due to impeachment has committed any offense while in office, the federal laws as per Sub-article (9) of Article 101 of the Constitution shall not prevent legal action against such an offense.
(8) A person removed from office due to impeachment as per this chapter shall not be entitled to any benefits from their position and shall not be eligible for future appointment or nomination to any public office.
(9) The House of Representatives shall conclude the impeachment proceedings within a maximum of five months from the date the motion is registered. If the term of the House of Representatives is less than five months, the Speaker may expedite the proceedings in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee.
(10) If an impeachment motion is registered when the term of the House of Representatives is less than five months, the Speaker may expedite the proceedings in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee as per the expedited procedure determined by the Business Advisory Committee.
(11) If the impeachment motion registered under Sub-rule (10) cannot be concluded even through the expedited procedure, or if the motion remains on record, it shall be considered a new impeachment motion for the newly elected House of Representatives. The House of Representatives shall receive the record within five months of its formation and make a necessary decision within the next five months.
164. Deemed to be Automatically Removed from Office: (1) If a motion of impeachment against the President or Vice-President is passed by at least two-thirds majority of the total members present in both Houses of the Federal Parliament as per Sub-article (1) of Article 101 of the Constitution, the President or Vice-President shall be deemed automatically removed from office.
(2) The Secretary-General shall inform the concerned President or Vice-President, the Government of Nepal, the Prime Minister, and the Council of Ministers about such removal from office.
(3) If the President or Vice-President removed from office due to impeachment has committed any offense while in office, the federal laws as per Sub-article (9) of Article 101 of the Constitution shall not prevent legal action against such an offense.
(4) A person removed from office due to impeachment as per this chapter shall not be entitled to any benefits from their position and shall not be eligible for future appointment or nomination to any public office.
165. Impeachment Against the Head or Official of a Constitutional Body: (1) If a motion of impeachment against the head or official of a constitutional body as per Sub-article (2) of Article 101 of the Constitution is to be presented, the grounds and reasons for impeachment shall be stated, and notice shall be given to the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary.
(2) "Official" for the purpose of this Rule means the Chief Justice or a Justice of the Supreme Court, a member of the Judicial Council, the Attorney General, or the head or official of any constitutional body of Nepal as per Sub-article (2) of Article 101 of the Constitution.
(3) If the House of Representatives is not in session, the member presenting the motion shall request the convening of a session as per Sub-article (3) of Article 93 of the Constitution within a maximum of fifteen days from the date the motion is registered, specifying the date and time for the meeting.
(4) After receiving the motion as per Sub-rule (1), the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall submit it to the Speaker. If the session is in progress, the date and time for discussion shall be specified within fifteen days, and if the session is not in progress, the first meeting after the session is convened shall be scheduled.
(5) After the Speaker calls the name as per Sub-rule (4), the proposing member shall present the motion of impeachment in the meeting. If they wish, they may present a statement before presenting the motion.
(6) After the motion is presented as per Sub-rule (4), the Speaker shall determine the time limit for discussion on the motion. After the discussion is concluded, the Speaker shall send the motion to the Impeachment Recommendation Committee within three days as per Rule 165.
(7) If, after preliminary investigation as per Sub-rule (6), the committee finds reasonable and sufficient grounds for impeachment against the concerned person, it may submit a recommendation for impeachment. If one-fourth of the total members present in the House of Representatives support such a recommendation presented to the House for decision, the impeachment proceedings shall commence.
(8) If the committee finds reasonable and sufficient grounds for impeachment against the concerned person after preliminary investigation as per Sub-rule (7), it may submit a recommendation for impeachment. If one-fourth of the total members present in the House of Representatives support such a recommendation presented to the House for decision, the impeachment proceedings shall commence.
(9) While impeachment proceedings are underway as per Sub-rule (8) and (7), the Chief Justice or a Justice of the Supreme Court, a member of the Judicial Council, the Attorney General, or the head or official of any constitutional body against whom impeachment proceedings are initiated shall not perform their duties of office until the proceedings are concluded.
(10) The Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall inform the concerned bodies and officials about the suspension of duties as per Sub-rule (9) under the direction of the Speaker.
166. Motion of Impeachment Recommendation Committee: (1) A motion of impeachment recommendation committee shall be formed in the House of Representatives if there are grounds and reasons for impeachment against the head or official of a constitutional body as per Sub-article (2) of Article 101 of the Constitution.
(2) The impeachment recommendation committee shall consist of eleven members.
(3) The Speaker shall present a motion for the formation of the impeachment recommendation committee in the meeting after consulting with the Business Advisory Committee.
(4) The members of the impeachment recommendation committee shall elect a chairperson from among themselves.
167. Procedure of the Impeachment Recommendation Committee: (1) After receiving the motion of impeachment, the impeachment recommendation committee shall commence its investigation as soon as possible.

168. Report of the Impeachment Recommendation Committee: (1) The impeachment recommendation committee shall submit its report with recommendations to the House after completing its investigation.
(2) After the report is submitted to the meeting, a copy of the report shall be distributed to all members.
169. Consideration of the Report of the Impeachment Recommendation Committee: (1) The Chairperson of the impeachment recommendation committee or, in his absence, any member designated by the Speaker, shall present a motion for consideration of the committee's report in any meeting held forty-eight hours after the report is submitted.
(2) After the motion as per Sub-rule (1) is presented, the report shall be discussed in the meeting.
(3) During the discussion as per Sub-rule (2), any member may present a motion to send the report back to the impeachment recommendation committee for further investigation regarding any specific matter.
(4) If the motion to send the report back to the impeachment recommendation committee as per Sub-rule (3) is approved, the report shall be sent to the committee, and the committee shall re-examine it and submit its report to the meeting within seven days.
170. Motion to Approve the Report of the Impeachment Recommendation Committee: (1) After the conclusion of the discussion on the report as per Rule 168, or after the impeachment recommendation committee's report is resubmitted to the meeting as per Sub-rule (4) of the same Rule, the Chairperson of the committee or, in his absence, any member designated by the Speaker, may present a motion to approve the recommendations mentioned in the report.
(2) If a motion is presented as per Sub-rule (1), any member may present an amendment to the report, if the Speaker deems it appropriate.
(3) After the discussion on the motion presented as per Sub-rule (1) and any amendments presented as per Sub-rule (2), the Speaker shall finalize the amendments and present the report with the approved recommendations to the meeting for decision.

(5) If the impeachment motion against any official is passed by at least two-thirds majority of the total members present in the House of Representatives, the concerned official shall be deemed removed from office.
(6) The Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall inform the President, the Prime Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the concerned official about the decision of the impeachment motion.
(7) If the President or Vice-President removed from office due to impeachment has committed any offense while in office, the federal laws as per Sub-article (9) of Article 101 of the Constitution shall not prevent legal action against such an offense.
(8) A person removed from office due to impeachment as per this chapter shall not be entitled to any benefits from their position and shall not be eligible for future appointment or nomination to any public office.
(9) The House of Representatives shall conclude the impeachment proceedings within a maximum of five months from the date the motion is registered. If the term of the House of Representatives is less than five months, the Speaker may expedite the proceedings in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee.
(10) If an impeachment motion is registered when the term of the House of Representatives is less than five months, the Speaker may expedite the proceedings in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee as per the expedited procedure determined by the Business Advisory Committee.
(11) If the impeachment motion registered under Sub-rule (10) cannot be concluded even through the expedited procedure, or if the motion remains on record, it shall be considered a new impeachment motion for the newly elected House of Representatives. The House of Representatives shall receive the record within five months of its formation and make a necessary decision within the next five months.
171. Motions Shall Be as Per This Chapter: Notwithstanding anything written in any other chapter of these Rules, impeachment proceedings shall be conducted as per the provisions of this chapter.
Chapter-20
Confidential Meeting of the House
172. Confidential Meeting of the House: (1) If the Prime Minister requests the Speaker to hold a confidential discussion on any matter related to national security or national crisis, and if the Speaker deems it appropriate, the Speaker may decide to hold such a discussion in a confidential meeting.
(2) During a confidential meeting of the House, no person other than the members of the House shall be allowed to be present in the meeting chamber. However, the Speaker may permit marshals or other staff of the Secretariat to be present in the meeting chamber.
(3) The Speaker or the person authorized by the Speaker shall maintain and publish a brief record of the proceedings and decisions of the confidential meeting in a manner deemed appropriate. No person other than the Speaker or the authorized person shall keep or publicize any information regarding the proceedings of the confidential meeting.
(4) The procedure for conducting a confidential meeting shall be as determined by the Speaker.
(5) If the Prime Minister or any member authorized by him deems it necessary to keep the proceedings of a confidential meeting confidential, they may present a motion to the Speaker requesting that the proceedings of the confidential meeting not be kept confidential.
(6) If the motion as per Sub-rule (5) is approved, the Secretary shall prepare the details of the proceedings and decisions of the confidential meeting and publish them as directed by the Speaker.
