175. Assignment of Additional Subjects: Subjects not covered in Rule 173 may be assigned by the Speaker as deemed appropriate, ensuring they fall within the scope of a committee. If a subject falls within the scope of more than one committee, the Speaker may, in consultation with the Chairpersons of the concerned committees, direct them to hold a joint meeting.
176. Formation of Subject Committees: (1) The Speaker shall nominate a maximum of twenty-seven members for each subject committee as per Rule 173, with the consent of the political parties represented in the House of Representatives, excluding ex-officio members.
(2) A member whose interests conflict with the scope of the committee shall not be nominated to the concerned committee.
Clarification: For the purpose of this sub-rule, "matter of conflicting interest" means a subject matter where interests conflict as per prevailing laws.
(3) The Prime Minister and the concerned minister shall be ex-officio members of the committee related to their portfolio.
(4) When nominating members to the committee, proportional representation shall be ensured based on the number of members of political parties represented in the House, including women, Dalits, indigenous nationalities, backward regions, Muslims, Madhesis, Khas-Arya, Tharus, minority communities, and marginalized groups.
(5) Except for ministers, no member shall be a member of more than one subject committee at the same time.
(6) Notwithstanding anything written in Sub-rule (5), any member may attend the meeting of a committee they are not a member of, if they wish, after informing the Chairperson of the committee at least one day before the meeting. However, they shall not have the right to vote in such a committee.
177. Election of Chairperson: (1) Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, the election of the Chairperson of a committee shall be held on a day and time specified by the Speaker. The Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall publish the notice thereof at least forty-eight hours before the election.
(2) By 4:00 PM on the day preceding the day set for the election of the Chairperson, any member wishing to propose a candidate for the post of Chairperson shall submit the proposal in the format specified in Schedule-3 to the Secretary.
(3) After the proposer submits the proposal as per Sub-rule (2), the supporting member shall support it.
(4) If only one proposal is received as per Sub-rule (2), the proposed member shall be declared the Chairperson unopposed after the proposer and supporting members have spoken. If more than one proposal is received, after all supporting members have spoken, the Speaker shall present the proposals for decision to the committee in order.
(5) When presenting proposals for decision as per Sub-rule (4), the Speaker shall ask members to say "Aye" or "No" in favor of the proposal. The member who secures the majority shall be declared elected as Chairperson.
(6) If more than one proposal is presented for decision as per Sub-rule (4), the member proposed in the proposal that is approved shall be declared elected as Chairperson, and the remaining proposals shall not be presented for decision.
(7) A member who is an ex-officio member shall not have the right to vote in any committee they are a member of. However, this Rule shall not prevent them from casting a casting vote in case of a tie.
(8) An ex-officio member may vote in only one committee they are a member of, and shall inform the Speaker of the committee in which they will vote within twenty-four hours of the publication of the notice. However, an ex-officio member who is not a member of the House of Representatives shall not have the right to vote.
(9) No minister shall be eligible to be elected as Chairperson of a committee or to chair a committee meeting.
(10) In the absence of the Speaker or the Chairperson, the senior member present among the committee members shall chair the meeting.
(11) If the senior member is absent, the next senior member present shall chair the committee meeting.
(12) The elected Chairperson of the committee shall take the oath of office and secrecy before the Speaker in the format specified in Schedule-4.
(13) When electing the Chairperson of a committee as per this chapter, the principle of proportional representation shall be applied to ensure at least one-third representation of women in the subject committees.
(14) Other procedures related to the election of the committee chairperson shall be as determined by the Speaker.
178. Term of Office of Subject Committees and Vacancy of Chairperson and Member: (1) The term of office of each subject committee as per Rule 173 shall be for the duration of the House of Representatives. However, the Speaker may, with the consent of the House of Representatives, make changes or additions to the members.
(2) The post of Chairperson or member of a committee shall become vacant in the following circumstances:-
(a) If the member ceases to be a member,
(b) If the member becomes a minister,
(c) If the member resigns,
(d) If a motion is passed by a two-thirds majority of the total members of the committee stating that the member has not fulfilled their responsibilities honestly.
(3) The post of a member of a committee shall become vacant in the following circumstances:-
(a) If the member ceases to be a member,
(b) If the member becomes a minister,
(c) If the member resigns from their post,
(d) If the member ceases to be a member due to changes as per Sub-rule (1).
(4) If the post of committee Chairperson becomes vacant, the election shall be held as per Rule 176, and if the post of member becomes vacant, the nomination shall be made as per Sub-rule (1) of Rule 175.
(5) If the post of committee Chairperson becomes vacant as per Sub-rule (2), the election shall be held within fifteen days of the vacancy.
179. Functions, Duties, and Authority of Subject Committees: (1) The functions, duties, and authority of each subject committee within its scope as specified in Rule 173 shall be as follows:-
(a) To discuss bills related to ministries, commissions, and bodies within the committee's scope clause by clause and submit a report thereon.
(b) To evaluate the policies, programs, resource management, and other activities of ministries, departments, and subordinate bodies, and submit a report with appropriate comments and recommendations, including directives to the concerned bodies.
(c) To examine the revenue and expenditure estimates of ministries, departments, and subordinate bodies, and to provide necessary directives and submit a report with their opinion regarding the methods for preparing annual estimates, alternative policies, and the extent of economy that can be achieved in the expenditure estimates.
(d) To study the steps taken by the Government of Nepal to fulfill the commitments and assurances made by ministers in the meeting from time to time, provide necessary directives to the concerned bodies, and submit a report to the meeting.
(e) To monitor and evaluate the utilization of public property related to the scope of the concerned bodies, and if there is any misappropriation, to provide necessary directives and submit a report to the meeting.
(f) To examine whether laws, rules, and regulations made by the government are in accordance with the Constitution, Acts, and prevailing laws, and to provide necessary directives to the concerned bodies after evaluation.
(g) To investigate reports submitted by commissions or committees formed for investigation from time to time, and to provide necessary opinions, advice, suggestions, and directives to the concerned bodies.
(h) To hear complaints received from the general public within its scope, and to provide necessary opinions, advice, suggestions, and directives.
(i) To monitor and evaluate the work performed by ministries, departments, and other bodies within its scope, and to provide necessary opinions, advice, suggestions, and directives.
(j) To conduct work related to measuring law implementation.
(k) To monitor and evaluate the performance of constitutional bodies within its scope, provide opinions, advice, suggestions, and directives, and discuss annual reports to provide suggestions.
(l) To obtain progress reports within thirty days on the implementation of directives, opinions, advice, and suggestions given by the committee. If the implementation is not satisfactory, the committee may review the received information and reconsider.
(m) To monitor and review the implementation of directives given by the committee and submit a report thereon.
(n) If it deems necessary, to submit reports of constitutional bodies to the House for discussion and to provide suggestions.
(o) To perform any other tasks assigned by the House.
(p) To conduct its activities within the framework of the budget and programs approved by the Speaker, based on the committee's recommendations.
(2) While performing their duties, subject committees may consult with representatives of the concerned ministries, departments, commissions, and bodies, and with experts on the relevant subjects as needed.
(3) Representatives of the concerned bodies and experts shall be present in the committee meetings and provide accurate information.
(4) Ministers shall be present during discussions on bills in the committee. Ministers shall be mandatorily present during other discussions as needed.
(5) The concerned bodies shall provide information on the status of implementation of directives given by the committee to the committee regularly. If the directives are not implemented, the concerned bodies shall provide a clear reason to the committee for not doing so.
(6) Laws and related documents made under delegated legislation shall be mandatorily provided to the committee within thirty days.
(7) Subject committees may formulate and implement work plans and schedules as needed to efficiently carry out their responsibilities.
(8) The committee may examine the audit irregularities mentioned in the annual report of the Auditor General and the work performed by the concerned bodies in relation thereto, and may conduct studies and provide necessary directives.
(9) Committee members may visit relevant locations as part of their committee work. However, they must obtain prior permission from the Speaker for such visits, clearly stating the reasons.
(10) The committee shall submit its annual report to the House at least fifteen days before the end of the session, and other reports at any time.
180. Matters to be Considered Regarding Delegated Legislation: (1) While discussing delegated legislation, the committee shall consider the following matters:-
(a) Whether the rules are in accordance with the objective of the Constitution or the Act,
(b) Whether the Government or the concerned body has made delegated legislation as delegated by the Parliament,
(c) Whether the matters specified by the Act are included in the delegated legislation,
(d) Whether the delegated legislation imposes or levies any tax,
(e) Whether the delegated legislation directly or indirectly interferes with the jurisdiction of the court as per the arrangement made by the Parliament,
(f) Whether the delegated legislation is retrospective, or whether any provision prohibits it,
(g) Whether the delegated legislation requires expenditure,
(h) Whether the delegated legislation is within the scope of authority granted by the Constitution or the Act,
(i) Whether the delegated legislation has been unnecessarily delayed in its publication and submission to the Secretariat,
(j) Whether any clarification is needed to explain the delegated legislation.
(2) In addition to the matters mentioned in Sub-rule (1), the committee may include the following in its report:-
(a) Recommendations, with reasons, if any rule is found to require complete or partial repeal or amendment,
(b) Directives given by the Government of Nepal to the concerned bodies from time to time to fulfill commitments and assurances made in the meeting.
(3) If any other related matter needs to be included in the report as per Sub-rule (2), the committee shall disclose such matters to the House.
(4) Any member may present an amendment to the report submitted by the committee, as deemed appropriate by the Speaker.
(5) The Speaker shall set the date and time for discussion on the report submitted by the committee and any amendments thereto.
(6) At the conclusion of the discussion on the report and amendments, the concerned minister shall answer the questions raised.
(7) Depending on the situation, the report and the approved amendments shall be presented to the House for decision, either in their original form or with the approved amendments.
(8) The Secretary shall inform the concerned minister about the decision made as per Sub-rule (7).
(9) The concerned minister shall implement the recommendations given by the committee.
(10) The concerned minister shall inform the House about the amendments or repeals made during the implementation of the committee's recommendations.
181. Special Committees: (1) Special committees may be formed in the House of Representatives as needed for special, sensitive, or serious nature bills or other matters.
(2) If a special committee needs to be formed as per Sub-rule (1), the Speaker shall present a proposal to the meeting including the names of the members, the work to be done by the committee, and the time limit for its completion, after consulting with the Business Advisory Committee.
182. Committee Meetings: (1) Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, the Chairperson of the committee may convene committee meetings as needed. However, if one-fourth of the committee members submit a written request to the Chairperson stating that it is necessary to hold a meeting to discuss urgent matters, the Chairperson shall specify the date and time for the meeting within five days.
(2) The Chairperson of the committee, or in his absence, a member chosen by him, shall chair the committee meeting.
(3) The member chosen by the Chairperson to chair the committee meeting shall have all the powers of the Chairperson.
(4) If it is necessary for the committee or sub-committee to meet outside the premises of the Parliament, the Chairperson may obtain written permission from the Speaker to do so.
183. Quorum: (1) Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, the quorum for a committee meeting shall be one-fourth of the total number of members present.
(2) If the quorum is not met, the Chairperson shall adjourn the meeting or postpone the committee meeting until the quorum is met.
(3) If the quorum is not met, the Chairperson shall inform the Speaker about it.
184. Action for Continuous Absence: If a member of a committee is continuously absent from five consecutive meetings without providing a reason, the Speaker may remove the member from the committee upon the recommendation of the committee, and the meeting shall be informed accordingly.
185. Committee Decisions: (1) Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, committee decisions shall be made by a majority of the members present. In case of a tie, the Chairperson shall have the casting vote.
(2) The decision of the committee meeting shall be certified by the Chairperson and the Secretary of the committee.
186. Formation of Sub-Committees: (1) The committee may form sub-committees from among its members to conduct or study specific matters within its scope or to submit reports.
(2) When forming a sub-committee, the work to be done by the sub-committee and the time limit for its completion shall be specified.
(3) A member of a sub-committee shall obtain prior approval from the Chairperson to visit any location for the purpose of study and submitting a report.
187. Entry of Concerned Officials or Experts: (1) When discussing any matter in a committee or sub-committee, if the Speaker deems it necessary, the concerned minister may bring government officials or experts to the committee with the Speaker's permission to provide clarification on the matter. It shall be the duty of such officials or experts to be present in the committee and provide clear information.
(2) The committee may invite representatives of concerned parties or interest groups and experts to seek their opinions.
(3) It shall be the duty of the representatives of concerned parties or interest groups and experts to be present in the committee and provide clear information as required.
188. Shortening of Discussion: If the Speaker feels that the discussion in the committee is unnecessarily prolonged, whether a time limit has been set or not, the Speaker may shorten the discussion.
189. Authority to Summon Documents and Concerned Persons or Government Officials: (1) The committee may summon documents or require the presence of concerned persons or government officials as needed.
However, if the minister believes that providing such information would be contrary to national security, peace and order, or public or national interest, they shall inform the committee of the reasons and may not table the documents.
(2) The committee may question or interrogate the present persons or government officials as needed.
(3) The decision of the committee in this regard shall be final.
(4) The committee shall submit its report to the House. The Chairperson or, in his absence, the nominated member of the committee shall present the report to the meeting.
(5) The concerned minister shall present the report of the committee to the meeting and regularly provide information on the status of its implementation.
(6) The committee may conduct monitoring and evaluation of its annual report and submit a report thereon to the meeting.
(7) If the House assigns any subject for discussion based on the report submitted by the committee, the Speaker may seek notice from the concerned committee's Chairperson within two days of the report being presented.
(8) If a notice is received as per Sub-rule (7), the Speaker shall grant permission to the concerned committee's Chairperson to present a motion for discussion within two days of receiving the notice.
(9) After the motion is presented, the Speaker may set a time limit for the discussion. At the conclusion of the discussion, the concerned minister shall answer the questions raised.
190. Authority to Maintain Order and Discipline in the Committee: (1) The Chairperson of the committee shall have all the powers of the Speaker as per these Rules to maintain peace, order, and discipline in the committee meetings and to ensure the smooth operation of the committee.
(2) If any member is expelled or suspended from a committee meeting, the Chairperson shall inform the Speaker accordingly.
191. Notice of Absence: If a member of a committee is continuously absent from five consecutive meetings without providing a reason, they shall submit a written notice to the Chairperson, stating the reason. If the absence is for more than five consecutive meetings, the Speaker shall be informed accordingly.
192. Secretariat of the Committee: (1) A secretariat shall be established under each committee.
(2) The Secretary-General shall appoint a first-class gazetted officer of the Secretariat to serve as the Secretary of the committee.
(3) If a first-class gazetted officer is not available, there shall be no objection to appointing a senior second-class gazetted officer.
(4) The Secretary of the committee may request necessary information and cooperation from the concerned ministries and bodies to facilitate the committee's work.
193. Can Give Opinion: The Secretary-General, Secretary, or Secretary of the committee may, with the permission of the Chairperson, express their opinion on matters under consideration in the committee meeting.
194. Shall Not Participate in Discussion and Decision: A member of a committee shall not participate in the discussion and decision of any matter if they have a direct personal interest or stake in that matter.
195. Scope of Committee: (1) A committee shall only conduct discussions and monitoring related to matters falling within its scope.
(2) If a matter falls outside the committee's scope, the committee shall conduct study and discussion related to it only after obtaining prior approval from the Speaker.
(3) Any dispute regarding the scope of the committee shall be finally decided by the Speaker.
196. Meeting of Committee Chairpersons: The Speaker may convene a meeting of committee chairpersons to evaluate the effectiveness of the committee's work. The Secretary of the committee may also participate in such meetings.
Chapter-22
Committee on Privileges
197. Formation of Committee on Privileges: (1) A Committee on Privileges shall be formed in the House of Representatives as per Article 103 of the Constitution. The Speaker may nominate up to fifteen members to such a committee in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee. However, no minister shall be a member of the Committee on Privileges.
(2) When nominating members to the Committee on Privileges, representation shall be ensured from all political parties represented in the House of Representatives, considering gender, ethnicity, experience, and regional knowledge, in a proportional manner.
(3) The members of the Committee on Privileges shall elect a chairperson from among themselves.
(4) The term of office of the Chairperson of the committee shall be for the duration of the House of Representatives.
(5) The elected Chairperson of the committee shall take the oath of office and secrecy before the Speaker in the format specified in Schedule-4.
198. Rules to Apply: The provisions regarding the vacancy of the Chairperson or member, filling of vacant posts, chairing arrangements, quorum, committee meetings, and decisions shall apply as necessary to the Committee on Privileges.
199. Notice of Question Regarding Privileges: (1) If any member feels that their privileges have been breached, they shall submit a written notice to the Secretary, stating the grounds for the breach of privileges. If the notice is based on any document, such a document shall be attached. The notice shall clearly state the nature of the breach of privileges and the place where it occurred.
(2) The Secretary shall promptly inform the Speaker and the Chairperson of the Committee on Privileges about the notice received as per Sub-rule (1), and the Chairperson shall convene a meeting as directed by the Speaker.
200. Conditions for Raising Questions Regarding Privileges: A question regarding the breach of privileges must relate to a direct incident that occurred during the current meeting or after the conclusion of the previous meeting.
201. Preliminary Investigation of Questions Regarding Privileges: (1) The Committee on Privileges shall conduct a preliminary investigation into questions regarding the breach of privileges.
(2) In the course of the preliminary investigation, the Committee on Privileges may question the concerned person and demand the submission of documentary evidence.
(3) If, upon preliminary investigation, the Committee on Privileges finds reasonable grounds for a breach of privileges, it shall present a report with the reasons to the Speaker and the concerned member. If it does not find reasonable grounds, it shall provide information to the Speaker and the concerned member.
202. Method of Raising Questions Regarding Privileges: (1) A member wishing to raise a question regarding the breach of privileges shall, after obtaining permission from the Speaker, present a concise statement of the matter to the meeting and seek permission to raise the question.
(2) If any member opposes the question regarding the breach of privileges, the Speaker shall ask the opposing and supporting members to stand up. If twenty or more members stand up, permission to present the motion shall be deemed granted, and if fewer than twenty members stand up, permission shall be deemed not granted.
203. Entrusting Questions to the Committee on Privileges: (1) If permission is granted by the meeting to raise a question regarding the breach of privileges, the member may present a motion to the meeting stating that the question be considered or sent to the committee.
(2) After the motion as per Sub-rule (1) is presented, the Speaker shall set a time limit for discussion on the motion.
(3) After the discussion on the motion as per Sub-rule (2) is concluded, the proposing member may withdraw the motion with the Speaker's permission. If the motion is not withdrawn, the Speaker shall present it for decision to the meeting.
(4) If the motion is approved as per Sub-rule (3), the Speaker may use the powers specified in Rule 204 and other relevant rules to decide on the question regarding privileges.
(5) If the motion is approved, the Speaker shall send the question along with the necessary documents to the committee for investigation and submission of a report.
204. Procedure and Authority of the Committee on Privileges: (1) After receiving the question along with the motion as per Sub-rule (4) of Rule 203, the Committee on Privileges shall commence its investigation as soon as possible.
(2) The Chairperson of the Committee on Privileges shall manage the investigation procedures as directed by the Speaker.
(3) In the course of the investigation, the Committee on Privileges may issue arrest warrants, summon witnesses, collect documentary evidence, or take depositions.
(4) The Committee on Privileges may, if it deems necessary, keep the person accused of breach of privileges in custody for a maximum of three months. If the committee orders anyone to be kept in custody, it shall inform the meeting accordingly.
(5) If the committee revokes the custody order, the person kept in custody shall be released immediately.
205. Report of the Committee on Privileges: (1) The Committee on Privileges shall investigate each question entrusted to it, give the accused person a reasonable opportunity to present their defense, consider all facts, and submit a report to the meeting with recommendations, stating whether or not the privileges have been breached.
(2) Before the discussion on the report as per Sub-rule (1) takes place, the report shall be distributed to all members at least one day before the meeting.
206. Consideration of the Report of the Committee on Privileges: (1) After the report is presented to the meeting, the Chairperson of the Committee on Privileges or, in his absence, the senior member designated by the Speaker, shall present a motion for consideration of the report.
(2) After the motion as per Sub-rule (1) is presented, the report shall be discussed in the meeting.
207. Amendments Can Be Presented: (1) During the discussion on the report as per Sub-rule (2) of Rule 206, any member may present an amendment to send the report back to the Committee on Privileges for further investigation.
(2) After a brief discussion on the amendment as per Sub-rule (1), it shall be presented to the meeting for decision.
(3) If the motion to send the report back to the committee as per Sub-rule (1) is approved, the report shall be sent back to the committee, and the committee shall re-examine it and submit its report to the meeting within seven days.
208. Motion to Approve the Report of the Committee on Privileges: (1) After the conclusion of the discussion on the report as per Rule 206, or after the report is resubmitted to the meeting as per Sub-rule (3) of Rule 207, any member may present a motion to approve the recommendations mentioned in the report.
(2) If a motion is presented as per Sub-rule (1), any member may present an amendment to the report, if the Speaker deems it appropriate.
(3) After the discussion on the motion presented as per Sub-rule (1) and any amendments presented as per Sub-rule (2), the Speaker shall finalize the amendments and present the question of breach of privileges to the meeting for decision.
209. Can Grant Pardon or Reduce Punishment: (1) If a person convicted in a question of privileges is sentenced as per the decision of the House under Sub-article (8) of Article 103 of the Constitution, the convicted person may submit a petition for pardon through the Speaker.
(2) The Speaker shall present the petition received as per Sub-rule (1) to the meeting. If the meeting is satisfied with the apology made by the convicted person, it may grant a pardon or reduce the imposed punishment.
Chapter-23
Motion Stating that the Speaker or Deputy Speaker Has Not Acted Appropriately in Their Position
210. Motion Stating that the Speaker or Deputy Speaker Has Not Acted Appropriately in Their Position: (1) If any member feels that the Speaker or Deputy Speaker has not acted appropriately in their position, they shall submit a notice of the motion to the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary, with the support of at least one-fourth of the total members of the House of Representatives currently in session, as per clause (c) of Sub-article (6) of Article 91 of the Constitution.
(2) After receiving the motion as per Sub-rule (1), the Secretary shall submit the motion to the Deputy Speaker if it is against the Speaker, to the Speaker if it is against the Deputy Speaker, and to the senior member as per Sub-article (5) of Article 91 of the Constitution if it is against both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker. The date and time for discussion on such a motion shall be specified within seven days of the submission of the motion.
(3) The motion as per Sub-rule (1) shall be distributed to all members at least one day before the discussion.
211. Chairing the Meeting: If the motion is against the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker shall chair the meeting for the discussion on the motion. If the motion is against both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker, the senior member as per Sub-article (5) of Article 91 of the Constitution shall chair the meeting.
212. Discussion and Decision on the Motion: (1) On the date and time specified for the discussion, the proposing member shall present the motion after their name is called by the person chairing the meeting. If they wish, the accused Speaker or Deputy Speaker may also participate in the discussion and vote.
(2) After the motion is presented, the person chairing the meeting shall set the time limit for the discussion. After the time limit expires, the Speaker or Deputy Speaker against whom the motion is made shall present their statement regarding the allegations.
(3) If the proposing member wishes, they may withdraw the motion they presented with the permission of the House. If the proposing member does not wish to withdraw the motion, the motion shall be presented for decision to the House.
(4) The decision on the motion as per Sub-rule (3) shall be made by a division of votes, including signed votes.
(5) If the motion is passed by a two-thirds majority of the total members present in the House of Representatives, the concerned Speaker or Deputy Speaker shall be deemed removed from office.
Chapter-24
Notice of Absence, Resignation, and Vacancy of Seat
213. Notice of Absence: (1) If any member has to be absent from the meeting for ten consecutive meetings due to illness or circumstances beyond their control, as per clause (d) of Article 89 of the Constitution, they shall submit advance notice regarding the same to the House through the Speaker.
(2) If a member is unable to attend less than ten meetings of the House, they shall provide advance notice to the Speaker. If there are valid reasons for not being able to provide advance notice, the notice shall be submitted within three days of their return.
(3) The notice submitted as per Sub-rule (1) or (2) shall clearly state the period and reason for absence. Such notice may also be submitted through electronic means.
(4) The Speaker shall present the notice as per Sub-rule (1) to the meeting for approval, and the Speaker shall approve the notice as per Sub-rule (2).
214. Resignation: (1) The Speaker may resign from their post by submitting a resignation to the President. The Deputy Speaker or any member may resign from their post by submitting a resignation to the Speaker.
(2) Upon receiving the resignation as per Sub-rule (1), the person chairing the meeting shall read it out to the members. The resignation shall be published in the notice paper if the meeting is not in session.
215. Notice of Vacancy of Seat: (1) If the seat of a member becomes vacant as per Article 89 of the Constitution, the Speaker shall inform the House accordingly.
(2) If the House is not in session, the Speaker shall cause the information about the vacancy to be published in the notice paper.
(3) The Secretary shall inform the Election Commission and the Council of Ministers about the vacancy and shall arrange for its publication in the Nepal Gazette.
Chapter-24
Office of the Parliamentary Party
216. Office of the Parliamentary Party: (1) The parliamentary party office of the political party represented in the House of Representatives shall be located within the premises of the Secretariat.
(2) The operation of the office of the parliamentary party shall be managed by the Secretariat in consultation with the Speaker, based on the number of members in the party and the recommendations of the Business Advisory Committee.
217. Filling of Details Form: Each member of the House of Representatives shall fill out the personal details form in the format specified in Schedule-5 and submit it to the Secretariat within seven days of the commencement of these Rules. However, a member who has already submitted the personal details form shall not need to submit it again.
218. Political Parties Represented in the House of Representatives Must Provide Details: (1) The leader of the political party represented in the House of Representatives shall provide the following details to the Secretariat within seven days of the commencement of these Rules:-
(a) Name and details of the members of their party,
(b) Names and signatures of up to two members authorized to correspond with the Secretariat on behalf of the party, in the format specified in Schedule-6,
(c) A copy of the constitution or rules of the concerned political party,
(d) A copy of the constitution or rules of the concerned parliamentary party, if any.
Clarification: For the purpose of this chapter, "Party Leader" means the member elected by the party as its leader, and the word also includes any member authorized by the party leader to perform the functions of the party leader.
(2) If a political party is formed during the term of the House, the leader of that party shall provide the details as per Sub-rule (1) to the Secretariat within seven days of its formation.
(3) If there is any change in the details provided as per Sub-rule (1), the party leader shall inform the Secretariat of such change within seven days of the change occurring.
Chapter-26
Provisions Regarding Member Conduct and Monitoring
219. Code of Conduct to be Observed: (1) The Speaker, officials, and members of the House of Representatives shall observe the following code of conduct to fulfill their responsibilities and maintain public trust in their work:-
(a) To achieve the objectives of the House and fully comply with these Rules for that purpose,
(b) To behave in a manner consistent with public morality and conduct,
(c) To attend meetings of the House or committees they are members of regularly and participate actively, and exercise their right to vote,
(d) To perform their duties impartially, honestly, and responsibly,
(e) In all activities related to the meeting, members shall prioritize public objectives and, in case of conflict between personal and public interests, clearly stand for the public interest,
(f) Members shall not speak in exchange for personal financial gain, fees, remuneration, or rewards, nor participate in voting or discussions in such a manner,
(g) Confidential information and data obtained by members in their capacity as members shall be used only for the purpose of the meeting's business and shall not be used for personal financial gain or transacted with any other person or organization.
(h) If a member has a personal or private interest in any matter under consideration in the House or a committee they are a member of, they shall inform the meeting or committee and refrain from participating in the discussion on that matter.
(2) This code of conduct shall apply to all aspects of the public life of officials and members. However, it shall not be considered related to the personal or private life of officials and members.
220. Formation of the Monitoring Committee: (1) A Conduct Monitoring Committee shall be formed in the House of Representatives.
(2) The committee as per Sub-rule (1) shall be formed as follows:-
- Chairperson: Speaker
- Deputy Chairperson: Deputy Speaker
- Member: Leader of the Opposition
- Member: Up to eight members nominated by the Speaker in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee, based on proportional representation of political parties in the House of Representatives.
(3) The Secretary-General of the Federal Parliament shall serve as the Secretary of the committee.
221. Functions, Duties, and Authority of the Conduct Monitoring Committee: (1) The functions, duties, and authority of the Conduct Monitoring Committee shall be as follows:-
(a) To investigate allegations of violation of the code of conduct mentioned in Sub-rule (1) of Rule 219 by any member, based on public concerns or information provided to the committee by anyone.
(b) To collect necessary information from members and other persons regarding conduct.
(c) To collect necessary information from persons, organizations, or the media raising questions regarding conduct.
(d) To determine, based on the facts collected during the investigation of conduct-related questions, whether a member has violated conduct or not, and to submit a report with clear reasons.
(2) The Conduct Monitoring Committee may form sub-committees, including experts, as needed.
(3) The Conduct Monitoring Committee shall determine its own internal procedures.
(4) If an investigation into a member for violation of conduct is initiated under this Rule, the concerned member shall cooperate as necessary.
(5) If an investigation into a member for violation of conduct is initiated under this Rule, the Conduct Monitoring Committee shall give the concerned member an opportunity to present their defense.
(6) The report submitted by the Conduct Monitoring Committee in its meeting shall be kept in the records. A copy of the report shall be sent to the concerned member and the office of the parliamentary party.
Chapter-27
Statement by Minister, Tabling of Documents, and Resignation
222. Statement and Information by Minister: (1) A minister may make a statement or provide information in the meeting with the Speaker's permission on matters of public importance.
(2) Any member may ask questions focusing on the statement or information provided by the minister as per Sub-rule (1), with the Speaker's permission, and the concerned minister shall answer such questions.
223. Documents to be Tabled: (1) If a minister or proposer quotes any part of a government document, report, or its summary while making a statement or presenting a proposal in the meeting, such document or report shall be tabled in the meeting. However, if the minister believes that tabling such a document or report would be contrary to national security, peace and order, or public or national interest, they shall inform the House of the reasons and may not table the document or report.
(2) If the summary of any document or report is mentioned, the document or report shall not be tabled.
224. Statement by Minister Resigning: (1) A member or person resigning from the post of minister may make a statement in the meeting with the Speaker's permission regarding their resignation.
(2) No discussion shall take place on the statement made as per Sub-rule (1).
Chapter-28
Treaties
225. Presentation of Treaties: (1) If the approval, accession, ratification, or support of a treaty is required as per Article 279 of the Constitution, the concerned minister shall present the treaty to the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary, within seven days of receiving the notice, along with details of the treaty, including its nature, a certified copy of the authentic text, and its Nepali translation, stating the following:-
(a) The objective of the treaty for which approval, accession, ratification, or support is required, its main provisions, the reasons for Nepal being a party to such a treaty, and its justification,
(b) The national interest involved in such a treaty and the obligations to be fulfilled,
(c) The laws that need to be enacted to implement such a treaty, and details thereof,
(d) In the case of multilateral treaties, the number of parties, and the proposal regarding reservations made by Nepal,
(e) Any interpretation or opinion given by the mechanism under the treaty, and such interpretation or opinion,
(f) In the case of reservations, the reasons for the reservations and the proposal.
(2) After receiving the notice as per Sub-rule (1), the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall make the copy of the treaty available to the members at least five days before the meeting.
(3) The concerned minister shall make a statement in the meeting when presenting the treaty for approval, accession, ratification, or support.
(4) After the minister makes the statement as per Sub-rule (3), the Speaker shall set a time limit for general discussion on the treaty.
226. General Discussion on Treaties: (1) After the general discussion on the treaty as per Rule 225 is concluded, a member may present a motion in any subsequent meeting stating, "Let there be a general discussion on the treaty."
(2) During the discussion on the motion as per Sub-rule (1), the discussion shall be limited to the theoretical aspect of the treaty, including whether approval, accession, ratification, or support is required or not.
(3) At the conclusion of the discussion, the concerned minister shall answer the questions raised.
227. Amendments Regarding Reservations: (1) If, within seventy-two hours after the conclusion of the general discussion as per Rule 226, Nepal wishes to make reservations to any provision of the treaty or clarify any provision, the member wishing to present an amendment shall give notice of the amendment to the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary.
(2) The Speaker shall have the authority to accept, reject, or ask the concerned member to improve any amendment, or to consolidate and accept amendments with similar intent.
(3) If there are no reservations made under the provisions of a treaty, no amendments may be presented to such a treaty.
228. Detailed Discussion on Treaty Provisions with Amendments: After the conclusion of the general discussion on the treaty, the proposing minister may present one of the following motions in any subsequent meeting:-
(a) That the provisions of the treaty be discussed,
(b) That the treaty be sent to a committee for detailed discussion with amendments.
229. Detailed Discussion on Treaty Provisions: (1) During the detailed discussion on the treaty provisions, including reservations, the discussion shall generally proceed in order, and the member called by the Speaker or the member authorized by them may present the amendment.
(2) For each provision with reservations or clear provisions, the Speaker shall present a motion stating, "Let this provision be part of the treaty."
However, for the sake of time efficiency, the Speaker may allow discussion on a provision or related amendments collectively, and may present parts or provisions of the treaty for discussion in a different order.
230. Amendments Can Be Withdrawn: A member proposing an amendment may withdraw the amendment with the Speaker's permission.
231. Committee Report: After the detailed discussion on the treaty provisions is concluded in the committee, the Chairperson or, in his absence, the nominated member of the concerned committee shall submit the report of the committee's decision to the meeting.
232. Procedure After Presentation of Committee Report: (1) After the committee report is presented, the report shall be distributed to all members.
(2) Unless the Speaker orders otherwise, the proposing member may present a motion in any meeting held twenty-four hours after the distribution of the report, stating, "Let the treaty be considered along with the report."
(3) During the discussion on the motion as per Sub-rule (2), the discussion shall be limited to the provisions of the treaty and related matters.
233. Motion to Approve, Ratify, or Support a Treaty: (1) After the detailed discussion on the treaty in the meeting is concluded and the discussion on the committee report is concluded, the proposing member shall present a motion to approve the treaty.
(2) A treaty or agreement mentioned in Sub-article (2) of Article 279 of the Constitution, for which approval, accession, ratification, or support is required, must be passed by a majority of at least two-thirds of the total members present in the House of Representatives.
(3) For treaties or agreements mentioned in clauses (a) and (d) of Sub-article (2) of Article 279 of the Constitution, which are of a general nature and do not have a significant or long-term impact on the nation, approval, accession, ratification, or support may be granted by a simple majority of the members present in the meeting of the House of Representatives.
(4) After the motion to approve, ratify, or support a treaty as per Sub-rule (2) is passed, the Secretary shall send it to the National Assembly with a message.
(5) If a treaty originating in the National Assembly and passed by it is received with a message, the Secretary shall table it in the House and distribute a copy of the message to the members.
(6) After the copy of the message with the treaty is distributed as per Sub-rule (5), the proposing member may present a motion for consideration of the treaty in any meeting held two days after the distribution. However, if the Speaker deems it appropriate, they may grant permission to present such a motion in any meeting after the distribution of the copy of the message with the treaty.
(7) The procedure for discussing a treaty as per Sub-rule (6) shall be as per the procedure for discussing treaties presented in the House.
234. Information to be Sent: Information regarding whether a treaty has been approved, acceded to, ratified, or supported shall be sent by the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary, to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Finance.
Chapter-29
Provisions Regarding Approval of Proclamation or Order of Emergency
235. Approval of Proclamation or Order of Emergency: (1) If the President issues a proclamation or order of emergency in Nepal as per Sub-article (1) of Article 273 of the Constitution, the Prime Minister shall provide the Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary with notice of such proclamation or order within one month of its issuance.
(2) After receiving the notice of the proclamation or order as per Sub-rule (1), the Speaker shall specify the date and time for presenting the motion in the first meeting held after receiving the notice.
(3) The Prime Minister shall present the motion in the meeting after obtaining the Speaker's permission and presenting a statement regarding the grounds and reasons for issuing the proclamation or order of emergency.
(4) After the motion is presented as per Sub-rule (3), the Speaker shall set a time limit for discussion on the motion. At the conclusion of the discussion, the Prime Minister or a minister authorized by him shall answer the questions raised if the Prime Minister is unable to attend the meeting due to illness or circumstances beyond their control.
(5) After the discussion is concluded as per Sub-rule (4), the Speaker shall present the motion for decision to the meeting.
(6) The decision on the motion as per Sub-rule (5) shall be made by a division of votes, including signed votes.
(7) If the House of Representatives is not in session at the time the proclamation or order of emergency as per Sub-rule (1) is issued, a session shall be convened within a maximum of fifteen days from the date of issuance of such proclamation or order.
236. Motion to Extend the Term of Proclamation or Order of Emergency: The Prime Minister shall provide the Secretary-General with notice of the motion to extend the term of the proclamation or order of emergency as per Sub-article (6) of Article 273 of the Constitution.
(2) Other procedures related to the motion shall be as specified in Rule 235.
237. Information to be Provided to the Council of Ministers: The Secretary-General or, in his absence, the Secretary shall inform the Council of Ministers about whether the proclamation or order has been approved or not as per this chapter.
Chapter-30
Miscellaneous
238. Attorney General May Express Opinion: (1) If the Speaker deems it necessary, the Attorney General may be invited to the House to express an opinion on any legal question as per Sub-article (4) of Article 948 of the Constitution.
(2) No discussion shall take place on the opinion expressed by the Attorney General as per Sub-rule (1).
(3) The procedure for expressing the opinion as per Sub-rule (1) shall be as determined by the Speaker.
239. Secretary-General May Be Present: The Secretary-General may be present in the meeting of the House or its committee or sub-committee if requested by the meeting or committee, and may provide advice or directives to the Secretary or officials working in the committee or sub-committee.
240. Security of Records: (1) The Secretary shall ensure that the records of the decisions and proceedings of the House and its committees are kept secure.
(2) Records related to the House and committees shall be kept in the library of the Secretariat for study purposes.
(3) The Secretariat shall provide members with audio and video recordings of their speeches upon request.
241. Language: (1) The proceedings of the House of Representatives and its committees shall be conducted in the Nepali language written in the Devanagari script. Any member may use the language recommended by the Language Commission and decided by the Government of Nepal, and arrangements shall be made to keep a record thereof.
(2) Notwithstanding anything written in Sub-rule (1), if a member with a disability wishes to express their opinion through sign language, the Speaker may allow a helper to translate their views into sign language and present them in the meeting.
242. Dress Code and Emblem: (1) The dress code for members shall be as determined by the Speaker in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee.
(2) While determining the dress code as per Sub-rule (1), attention shall be paid to formal, traditional, and culturally appropriate attire that reflects the national identity, tradition, and culture.
(3) Members shall wear the emblem specified in Schedule-7. The emblem shall be respected.
243. Provisions Regarding the Secretariat: (1) A Secretariat shall exist as per Article 107 of the Constitution to assist in the legislative work, operation, and management of the Federal Parliament, and to provide necessary services and facilities to the officials and members.
(2) Other provisions related to the operation of the Secretariat shall be in accordance with the Constitution, prevailing laws of Nepal, and the regulations approved by the committee managing the operation and management of the Federal Parliament Secretariat.
244. Provisions Regarding Experts or Expert Groups: (1) To assist in the committee's work, experts or expert groups may be invited on an honorary or paid basis, with their terms and conditions of service specified by the committee's decision.
(2) The terms and conditions of service for invited experts who are to be paid remuneration shall be determined by the Secretariat as per the operational guidelines.
245. Meetings Can Be Held Using Technology: (1) If it is not possible to hold meetings in person due to natural disasters or epidemics, and if at least one-fourth of the members of the House agree that it is not possible to hold meetings in person, the Speaker may decide to hold meetings using technology as needed, in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee.
(2) If it is necessary for a committee meeting to be held as per Sub-rule (1), the Chairperson of the committee may obtain permission from the Speaker to hold the meeting.
(3) The procedures for meetings held as per Sub-rule (1) and (2) shall be as determined by the Speaker.
246. Legal Opinion: In case of any legal questions arising during the proceedings of the House or its committees, legal opinions may be sought from the legal advisor available at the Secretariat as well as from external legal experts. The legal advisor shall represent the House or committee in any legal disputes, whether in favor or against.
However, this Rule shall not prevent the House or committee from seeking the assistance of external legal experts for such purposes.
247. Information Regarding Arrest of Members: (1) If the House is informed that a member has been arrested, the Speaker shall immediately inform the House accordingly.
(2) If information as per Sub-rule (1) is received when the House is not in session, the Speaker shall cause a notice thereof to be posted on the Secretariat's notice board and made public.
(3) If a member is arrested in connection with a criminal case punishable by imprisonment for three years or more, or a case involving moral turpitude, and if they are in custody or absconding without serving the sentence, such a member shall be deemed suspended from their membership and shall not be able to perform any duties or enjoy any rights or immunities during the period of suspension. Their remuneration, service, and facilities shall also be suspended during that period.
Clarification: For the purpose of this sub-rule, "Court" means the District Court, High Court, and Supreme Court.
(4) If a member is convicted and sentenced to imprisonment in a criminal case, or if they have to serve a sentence or are arrested and have not served the sentence, or are absconding, such a member shall be deemed automatically suspended from their membership and shall not be able to perform any duties or enjoy any rights or immunities during the period they are in custody or absconding.
(5) If a member arrested as per Sub-rule (3) is acquitted or released from custody, the Speaker shall immediately inform the House. If the House is in session, the information shall be published on the notice board. If the House is not in session, the information shall be made public through the Secretariat's notice board. If the suspension of a member is revoked, their remuneration, service, and facilities shall be resumed.
248. Nomination of Members: Except as specified elsewhere in these Rules, members of the House of Representatives shall be nominated to committees, groups, associations, or bodies related to the House of Representatives by the Speaker, considering their knowledge, skills, interests, and the party structure in the House. The formation and procedures of such groups, associations, or bodies shall be as determined by the Speaker.
249. Authority to Regulate Entry: (1) The meeting chamber of the House shall generally remain open. Visitors shall be allowed to observe the proceedings.
(2) The Speaker shall have the authority to regulate and control entry, keeping in mind the convenience of visitors.
(3) The Speaker may arrange for the issuance of entry passes to regulate entry as needed.
(4) Visitors entering the meeting building with an entry pass issued as per Sub-rule (2) must comply with the conditions specified on the pass. If any person violates these conditions, they may be expelled from the meeting building by order of the Speaker.
250. Addressing the Meeting: (1) The Speaker may grant permission to the Head of State or Head of Government of any foreign country, or the Secretary-General of the United Nations, to address the meeting upon the request of the Government of Nepal.
(2) The Speaker shall arrange for the seating of the addressing dignitary to the right of the Speaker.
(3) The procedure for addressing the meeting as per Sub-rule (1) shall be as determined by the Speaker.
251. Suspension of Rules: (1) Any member may present a motion to the House of Representatives to suspend any rule of these Rules, stating the reason and seeking permission to do so, in order to facilitate the conduct of business. If the motion is passed, the rule shall be deemed suspended for the time being.
(2) A motion to suspend rules may generally be presented only to shorten the time limit for the passage of a bill.
252. Brief Details of Actions Taken: Brief details of the actions taken shall be distributed to the members of the House.
253. Format to be Provided: The Secretariat shall provide the format of motions as mentioned in various places of these Rules.
254. Can Formulate and Implement Work Schedule: The House, in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee and the committees, may formulate and implement work schedules to ensure the efficient conduct of its business.
255. Can Consult: The Speaker and members of the House may consult with former members of the House regarding their work and performance.
256. Information Flow: The interaction and lobby activities of the House with the media shall be managed for effective information flow.
257. Internal Procedures: The Speaker may, in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee, formulate internal procedures as needed.
258. Authority to Remove Obstacles: The Speaker shall have the authority to remove obstacles encountered in the application of these Rules and to issue necessary orders or directives in accordance with the Constitution and these Rules. Such orders or directives shall be considered equivalent to decisions made in the meeting.
259. Rules to Apply: Notwithstanding anything written in any prevailing law, these Rules shall apply as special laws to the House, committees, and members.
(2) These Rules shall remain in force as the special rights of the members of the House of Representatives.
260. Interpretation of Rules: The Speaker shall have the authority to interpret these Rules, and the Speaker's decision shall be final. The meeting shall be informed of such decisions.
261. Shall be Considered Internal Proceedings: The work and proceedings of the committee shall be considered internal proceedings of the House and the committee.
No questions shall be raised in any court regarding this.
262. Procedure Regarding Amendments: (1) If any member deems it necessary to amend these Rules, they shall submit a proposal with reasons and details to the Speaker.
(2) If the Speaker deems the notice as per Sub-rule (1) appropriate, they shall present a motion to the House for approval to form a drafting committee for the amendment.
(3) The committee formed as per Sub-rule (2) shall consist of members as determined by the Speaker in consultation with the Business Advisory Committee, and the committee members shall elect their Chairperson.
(4) After the committee submits its report, other procedures related to the amendment shall be followed as determined by the Speaker, except for the procedures related to bills.
263. Repeal and Savings: (1) The House of Representatives Rules of Procedure, 2079, have been repealed.
(2) The work and proceedings conducted under the House of Representatives Rules of Procedure, 2079, shall be deemed to have been conducted as per these Rules.

sections.name: Preface
sections.summary_en: The preface outlines the purpose of the House of Representatives Rules of Procedure, 2083, which is to regulate parliamentary conduct, committee operations, and address procedural obstacles, in accordance with Article 104(1) of the Constitution of Nepal.

sections.name: Chapter - 1 Preliminary
sections.summary_en: This chapter defines the brief name and commencement of the Rules of Procedure as "House of Representatives Rules of Procedure, 2083" and specifies that they come into force immediately. It also provides definitions for various terms used in the Rules, such as "Minister of Finance", "Chairing Member", "Unparliamentary Word", "Deputy Speaker", "Senior Member", "Table", "Official", "Premises", "House of Representatives", "Delegated Legislation", "Motion", "Proposing Member", "Meeting Chamber", "Minister", "Council of Ministers", "Marshal", "Secretary-General", "Secretary", "Secretariat", "House/Assembly/Meeting", "Member", "Treaty", "Chairperson", "Speaker", "Committee", and "Notice Paper".

sections.name: Chapter - 2 Convening and Operation of Sessions and Meetings of the House of Representatives
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the procedures for convening and concluding sessions, member attendance, seating arrangements, meeting operations and adjournments, and the mandatory presence of ministers. It also outlines the responsibilities of parliamentary party leaders in cooperating with the House's operation.

sections.name: Chapter - 3 Election of Speaker and Deputy Speaker and Nomination of Members to Chair Meetings
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines the process for electing the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, including the nomination procedure, eligibility criteria, voting methods, and the oath-taking ceremony. It also details the nomination of members to chair meetings in the absence of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.

sections.name: Chapter - 4 Meeting Procedures
sections.summary_en: This chapter covers the procedures for government and non-government business, the daily agenda, the role of the Business Advisory Committee, time limits for discussions, Zero Hour and Special Time, giving notice, amending notices, distributing papers, commencing meetings, and the rules to be observed by members during meetings and discussions, including relevance and order of speaking.

sections.name: Chapter - 4 Methods of Decision Making
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the methods by which decisions are made in the House, including decisions by voting, the process of presenting questions for decision, and the procedure for divisions. It specifies how votes are collected and counted.

sections.name: Chapter - 6 Order in Meetings
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines measures for maintaining order in meetings, including warnings, expulsion from meetings, suspension of members, the Speaker's special authority, actions that can be taken against members, and the authority to adjourn meetings.

sections.name: Chapter - 7 Address by the President and Policy and Program
sections.summary_en: This chapter describes the procedures related to the President's address to the House, the subsequent vote of thanks, and the discussion on the government's policy and program. It also mentions other business that can be transacted during this period.

sections.name: Chapter - 8 Question and Answer
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the procedures for question and answer sessions, including the types of questions that can be asked, the notice period, the list of questions, the time allocated for question and answer, and the conditions regarding questions. It also covers supplementary questions and the process of withdrawing or postponing questions.

sections.name: Chapter - 9 Direct Question and Answer with the Prime Minister
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines the procedure for direct question and answer sessions with the Prime Minister, specifying the time allocated, the conditions for asking questions, and stating that no discussion shall take place on the answers provided.

sections.name: Chapter - 10 Procedure Regarding Motions
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the procedures for presenting and discussing motions, including conditions for acceptability, setting discussion times, motions becoming invalid, withdrawing motions, and the process for urgent public importance and attention motions.

sections.name: Chapter - 11 Adjournment Motion
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines the procedure for presenting and discussing adjournment motions, including the notice requirements, conditions for presentation, seeking permission from the meeting, determining discussion time, and the conclusion of the discussion and decision.

sections.name: Chapter - 12 Resolution Motion
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the procedure for presenting and discussing resolution motions, including the conditions for their presentation, the process of seeking amendments, and the decision-making process. It also covers the monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of passed resolutions.

sections.name: Chapter - 13 Amendments to Motions
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines the conditions for presenting amendments to motions, the procedure for giving notice of amendments, and the acceptance of amendments. It also covers the process of presenting amendments.

sections.name: Chapter - 14 Ordinances
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the procedures for presenting ordinances, including the notice to reject an ordinance, the method of presenting such a motion, and the discussion and decision on the motion. It also covers the decision on ordinances and the process for replacing approved ordinances.

sections.name: Chapter - 14 Management Procedures
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines the procedures for managing bills, including the notice for permission to present a bill, the presentation of dependent bills, the exclusion of bills on the same subject, commentary on delegated legislation, distribution of bills, notice of opposition to motions seeking permission to present bills, motions seeking permission to present bills, general discussion on bills, obtaining public opinion, and the conclusion of general discussion.

sections.name: Chapter - 16 Procedure Regarding Estimates of Income and Expenditure
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the procedures related to the estimates of income and expenditure, including the presentation of annual estimates, discussion on these estimates, supplementary estimates, and expenditure estimates.

sections.name: Chapter - 17 Procedure Regarding Appropriation and Finance Bills
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines the procedures for appropriation bills, including the motion for reduction of expenditure, conditions and notices for such motions, decisions on motions for reduction of expenditure, restrictions on amendments, advance expenditure bills, finance bills, supplementary appropriation bills, and loan expenditure bills.

sections.name: Chapter - 18 Vote of Confidence and No-Confidence Motion
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the procedures for obtaining a vote of confidence and presenting a no-confidence motion against the Prime Minister, including the requirements for submitting notices, discussion procedures, and the decision-making process.

sections.name: Chapter - 19 Motion of Impeachment
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines the procedures for filing a motion of impeachment against the President or Vice-President, including the formation of investigation committees, their procedures, reports, and the process for considering and deciding on impeachment motions. It also covers impeachment against constitutional body officials and the consequences of impeachment.

sections.name: Chapter - 20 Confidential Meeting of the House
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the procedures for conducting confidential meetings of the House, including the conditions for holding such meetings, the participants, and the management and publication of records.

sections.name: Chapter - 21 Committees of the House of Representatives
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines the formation of subject committees and special committees, their scopes, the process of electing chairpersons, the term of office, functions, duties, and authority of subject committees, matters to be considered regarding delegated legislation, and provisions for special committees, committee meetings, quorum, action for absence, committee decisions, formation of sub-committees, and the entry of concerned officials or experts.

sections.name: Chapter - 22 Committee on Privileges
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the formation of the Committee on Privileges, the rules that apply, the procedure for giving notice of questions regarding privileges, preliminary investigations, methods of raising questions, entrusting questions to the committee, and the committee's procedure and authority, including its report and consideration thereof.

sections.name: Chapter - 23 Motion Stating that the Speaker or Deputy Speaker Has Not Acted Appropriately in Their Position
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines the procedure for presenting a motion stating that the Speaker or Deputy Speaker has not acted appropriately in their position, including the process for chairing the meeting and the discussion and decision on the motion.

sections.name: Chapter - 24 Notice of Absence, Resignation, and Vacancy of Seat
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the procedures for notifying absence from meetings, submitting resignations, and announcing vacancies of seats in the House of Representatives.

sections.name: Chapter - 24 Office of the Parliamentary Party
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines the provisions related to the office of the parliamentary party, including its location, operation, filling of details forms, and the requirement for political parties represented in the House to provide details.

sections.name: Chapter - 26 Provisions Regarding Member Conduct and Monitoring
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the code of conduct to be observed by members, the formation of the Conduct Monitoring Committee, and its functions, duties, and authority. It emphasizes ethical behavior and accountability.

sections.name: Chapter - 27 Statement by Minister, Tabling of Documents, and Resignation
sections.summary_en: This chapter covers the procedures for ministers to make statements, table documents, and resign. It outlines the requirements for providing information, tabling documents, and making statements upon resignation.

sections.name: Chapter - 28 Treaties
sections.summary_en: This chapter details the procedures for presenting treaties, conducting general discussions on them, making amendments regarding reservations, concluding discussions, and holding detailed discussions on treaty provisions. It also covers the withdrawal of amendments, committee reports, and the process for approving, ratifying, or supporting treaties.

sections.name: Chapter - 29 Provisions Regarding Approval of Proclamation or Order of Emergency
sections.summary_en: This chapter outlines the provisions related to the approval of proclamations or orders of emergency, including the procedure for presenting such motions and extending their terms, and informing the Council of Ministers.

sections.name: Chapter - 30 Miscellaneous
sections.summary_en: This chapter covers miscellaneous provisions, including the Attorney General expressing opinions, the Secretary-General's presence, security of records, language, dress code and emblems, provisions regarding the Secretariat, experts or expert groups, meetings using technology, legal opinions, information regarding arrest of members, nomination of members, regulation of entry, addressing the meeting, suspension of rules, brief details of actions, formats to be provided, work schedules, consultations, information flow, internal procedures, removal of obstacles, application of rules, interpretation of rules, internal proceedings, amendment procedures, repeal and savings, and schedules.

sections.name: Schedule - 6 Details Related to Political Party Members
